articles.title: Key moments from Burnham's first Commons session as PM
articles.summary: The PM pledges "more substantial change" during his first speech to MPs.
articles.body:
Andy Burnham pledges "more substantial change" during his first speech to MPs as prime minister.

He also pays tribute to his predecessor Keir Starmer - who earlier announced he will stand down as an MP.

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said the new prime minister will be judged on "what he actually delivers".

Watch: Starmer's kind send-off across the Commons in final PMQs

A warmer and less confrontational tone than usual was struck during Sir Keir Starmer's final PMQs appearance as prime minister.

Shocked and upset - Politicians react to Ann Widdecombe's death

The prime minister and opposition leader spoke after the police announced a murder investigation into the death of Ann Widdecombe.

Watch: Farage resigns to trigger by-election he will stand in

In a statement filmed by Reform UK Nigel Farage announced he will resign as an MP to trigger a by-election which he will stand in.

Watch: PM's former top aide on Starmer's first call with Trump

Trump was more 'funny' than he had been expecting, Morgan McSweeney told the BBC.

Watch: The day Labour's potential leadership race began to heat up

Political turmoil continued in Westminster on Thursday after Health Secretary Wes Streeting resigned Starmer's government saying he had "lost confidence" in his leadership.

Wes Streeting has resigned as health secretary, amid speculation that he could launch a Labour leadership bid.

BBC chief political correspondent Henry Zeffman explains what this could mean for a potential Labour leadership contest.

Watch: What next after the King's Speech?

BBC Chief Political Correspondent Henry Zeffman explains what is next for the government after the King's Speech.

Watch: Pomp and ceremony as King delivers speech in Parliament

King Charles III has unveiled the government's agenda in a speech to Parliament.

Watch: Resignations, drama and defiance at Downing Street

Sir Keir Starmer will meet Wes Streeting for talks after a day that saw his leadership come under significant pressure.

Watch: What next as PM fights for his job?

Over 80 Labour MPs have now urged Keir Starmer to quit immediately or draw up a timetable to leave.

Watch: Reporters shout questions at ministers leaving No 10

Several ministers were met with a barrage of questions about the PM's future after leaving a cabinet meeting.

Watch: Keir Starmer's message of defiance to his own party

'The message is clear' - Labour MPs on Keir Starmer's leadership

Henry Zeffman: Election results leave Starmer vulnerable

Tory leader Kemi Badenoch on calling out the PM

Green Party leader Zack Polanski: 'It's up to government to fund social care'

Watch: PM's ex-top aide on Mandelson revelations

Key moments as Morgan McSweeney gives evidence to MPs about Peter Mandelson's appointment as US ambassador.

My five-minute phone call with President Trump

Sarah Smith asked the president about King Charles's upcoming visit, the state of the so-called special relationship and the war with Iran.

Watch key moments from sacked Foreign Office chief's testimony

Sir Olly Robbins told MPs No 10 had a "dismissive approach" to Lord Peter Mandelson's security vetting.

articles.title: IEL abre mais de 500 vagas de estágio em cidades da Bahia | G1
articles.standfirst: Há vagas para áreas como Comunicação, Pedagogia, Arquitetura, Engenharia, Psicologia, Enfermagem e mais em diversas cidades do estado.
articles.summary: Há vagas para áreas como Comunicação, Pedagogia, Arquitetura, Engenharia, Psicologia, Enfermagem e mais em diversas cidades do estado. Bolsas chegam a R$ 2,4 mil.
articles.body:
Unidade do Sesi/IEL em Feira de Santana — Foto: Silvio Tito/Sistema FIEB

O Instituto Euvaldo Lodi (IEL) abre 551 vagas de estágio em diferentes cidades da Bahia. As oportunidades abrangem níveis médio, técnico e superior, com bolsas que variam de R$ 450 a R$ 2.400, dependendo da unidade e da área de atuação.

Os interessados devem realizar o cadastro no site do IEL , e manter sempre atualizado para facilitar a participação nos processos seletivos.

Confira as vagas disponíveis por região:

Salvador e Região Metropolitana — 339 vagas

Há vagas para áreas como Comunicação, Pedagogia, Arquitetura, Administração, Engenharia, Ciências Contábeis, Psicologia, Direito, Educação Física, Enfermagem, Farmácia, Tecnologia da Informação, Marketing, Recursos Humanos, além de cursos técnicos e para estudantes do ensino médio.

Há vagas para Administração, Arquitetura, Comunicação Social, Marketing, Contabilidade, Direito, Educação Física, Eletromecânica, Enfermagem, Engenharia, Pedagogia, além de cursos técnicos e ensino médio.

Há oportunidades para estudantes das áreas administrativa, atendimento, comercial, comunicação, contabilidade, educação, eletrotécnica, enfermagem, laboratório, logística, manutenção, produção e vendas.

Vitória da Conquista e região — 25 vagas

📍 Cidades: Vitória da Conquista, Jequié , Guanambi e Itapetinga .

Há vagas para Enfermagem, Pedagogia, Marketing, Ciências da Computação, Administração, Ciências Contábeis, Economia, Agropecuária, Meio Ambiente, Design, Recursos Humanos e Engenharia Civil.

Há vagas para Administração, Pedagogia, Ciências Contábeis, Educação Física, Economia, Logística, Gestão Comercial, Recursos Humanos, Letras, Secretariado, Matemática, Gestão Financeira, Agronomia, Enfermagem, Engenharia, Arquitetura, Biomedicina, Geografia, História e Segurança do Trabalho.

Há vagas para Administração, Engenharia Agronômica, Ciências Contábeis, Engenharia da Computação, Engenharia Civil, Engenharia Elétrica, Ensino Médio e cursos técnicos em Edificações, Segurança do Trabalho, Administração e Recursos Humanos.

Além das vagas de estágio, o IEL também oferece 20 oportunidades pelo programa Inova Talentos, voltado para profissionais com nível superior completo ou estudantes de graduação a partir do 5º semestre. As vagas são para as áreas de Engenharia e Tecnologia, com oportunidades em Salvador e Camaçari, na Bahia, em São Paulo e também na modalidade 100% remota. As bolsas variam de R$ 2.500 a R$ 5.500.

Veja mais notícias de Feira de Santana e região .

articles.title: O que fazer em Alagoas: Luiz Fernando Guimarães e Tony Allysson | G1
articles.standfirst: Programação entre sexta-feira (4) e segunda-feira (7) tem atrações em Maceió, Arapiraca, Piranhas e Maribondo.
articles.summary: A programação cultural de Alagoas traz Luiz Fernando Guimarães e Tony Allysson em eventos por Maceió, Arapiraca e Piranhas neste feriadão.
articles.body:
Luiz Fernando Guimarães e Tony Allysson. — Foto: Montagem/g1

Alagoas recebe uma programação cultural diversificada entre sexta-feira (4) e segunda-feira (7), com opções de música, teatro, cultura popular e eventos religiosos. Entre os destaques estão o festival Vozes do Velho Chico, em Piranhas , um show em homenagem a Belchior, em Arapiraca , e a comédia "Baixa Sociedade", com Luiz Fernando Guimarães, em Maceió .

O festival Vozes do Velho Chico volta a ocupar o Centro Histórico de Piranhas e as margens do Rio São Francisco nos dias 4 e 5 de setembro.

A programação reúne música autoral, cultura popular, cinema, literatura, teatro, palhaçaria e cortejos. A abertura acontece na sexta-feira (4), com atividades espalhadas pelas ruas do Centro Histórico.

A cantora alagoana Dona Flô apresenta um show em homenagem a Belchior no Teatro Hermeto Pascoal, no Sesc Arapiraca.

No repertório estão músicas que marcaram a trajetória do cantor e compositor cearense. A apresentação faz parte da Mostra Sesc das Artes e Cultura Popular.

Onde: Teatro Hermeto Pascoal, Sesc Arapiraca

Maribondo recebe um cortejo cultural em homenagem a Joana Gajuru, com participação de manifestações da cultura popular e folguedos.

A concentração será realizada em frente à Prefeitura Municipal. Em seguida, o cortejo percorrerá as ruas da cidade.

Concentração: 7h30, em frente à Prefeitura

Concerto no Instituto Histórico e Geográfico de Alagoas

O Salão Nobre do Instituto Histórico e Geográfico de Alagoas (IHGAL) recebe o concerto "Pixinguinha e A Harmonia para Viver, de Chiquinha Gonzaga".

A apresentação é aberta ao público e gratuita.

O estacionamento do Shopping Pátio Maceió recebe mais uma edição do Vem pra Cristo, encontro católico que reúne música, oração, pregações, testemunhos e celebrações religiosas.

Entre as atrações estão os cantores Tony Allysson e Naldo José, além de sacerdotes convidados.

Onde: estacionamento do Shopping Pátio Maceió

A comédia "Baixa Sociedade" chega a Maceió no feriado de 7 de setembro. O espetáculo tem no elenco Luiz Fernando Guimarães, Debora Ozório, Paulo Mathias Jr. e Bruna Trindade.

A peça aborda conflitos, relações e os limites dos personagens em busca de ascensão social.

articles.title: Eleições 2026: veja todos os candidatos a deputado federal no Rio Grande do Sul | G1
articles.standfirst: RS tem 457 candidatos na disputa por 31 vagas; votação será em 4 de outubro.
articles.summary: RS tem 457 candidatos na disputa por 31 vagas; votação será em 4 de outubro.
articles.body:
O Rio Grande do Sul (RS) tem 457 candidatos disputando 31 vagas na Câmara dos Deputados, em Brasília, nas Eleições 2026, segundo dados do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE).

A votação será realizada em 4 de outubro, em turno único — a eleição para a Câmara dos Deputados não tem 2º turno. As vagas são distribuídas entre partidos e federações pelo sistema proporcional, para mandatos de quatro anos.

A lista abaixo traz os nomes e os números de urna dos candidatos, enviados pelos partidos ao TSE, e também a situação de cada um: se estão concorrendo ou inaptos para concorrer, conforme decisão da Justiça Eleitoral.

O Brasil tem 158,7 milhões de eleitores aptos a votar neste ano, segundo dados do TSE. Os votos serão para presidente, governador, senador, deputado federal e deputado estadual (ou distrital, apenas no caso do Distrito Federal). Todos os cargos têm mandato de quatro anos, exceto o de senador, cujo mandato é de oito anos.

O Senado vai renovar 54 das 81 cadeiras (dois terços do total). E cada eleitor deve votar em dois candidatos diferentes.

Na lista do TSE, os candidatos são classificados em duas situações principais: concorrendo ou inapto.

Cassado com recurso, indeferido com recurso ou pedido não conhecido com recurso;

Em algumas listas, o mesmo candidato aparece mais de uma vez. O TSE informa que manterá os nomes duplicados, mas apontará apenas uma das opções como apta ("concorrendo") até o dia da eleição.

Esta reportagem foi produzida de modo automático com dados fornecidos pelo Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) ( clique aqui para saber mais) e pode ser atualizada em caso de mudança na lista de candidatos a deputado federal no Rio Grande do Sul. Caso você perceba algum erro, por favor nos informe por meio do formulário .

O Paraná (PR) tem 615 candidatos disputando 54 vagas na Assembleia Legislativa nas Eleições 2026, segundo dados do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE).

A votação será realizada em 4 de outubro, e as vagas são distribuídas entre partidos e federações pelo sistema proporcional, para mandatos de quatro anos.

O Brasil tem 158,7 milhões de eleitores aptos a votar neste ano, segundo dados do TSE. Os votos serão para presidente, governador, senador, deputado federal e deputado estadual (ou distrital, apenas no caso do Distrito Federal). Todos os cargos têm mandato de quatro anos, exceto o de senador, cujo mandato é de oito anos.

articles.body:
São Paulo (SP) tem 1427 candidatos disputando 94 vagas na Assembleia Legislativa nas Eleições 2026, segundo dados do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE).

A votação será realizada em 4 de outubro, e as vagas são distribuídas entre partidos e federações pelo sistema proporcional, para mandatos de quatro anos.

A lista abaixo traz os nomes e os números de urna dos candidatos, enviados pelos partidos ao TSE, e também a situação de cada um: se estão concorrendo ou inaptos para concorrer, conforme decisão da Justiça Eleitoral.

O Brasil tem 158,7 milhões de eleitores aptos a votar neste ano, segundo dados do TSE. articles.body:
Goiás (GO) tem 590 candidatos disputando 41 vagas na Assembleia Legislativa nas Eleições 2026, segundo dados do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE).

A votação será realizada em 4 de outubro, e as vagas são distribuídas entre partidos e federações pelo sistema proporcional, para mandatos de quatro anos.

A lista abaixo traz os nomes e os números de urna dos candidatos, enviados pelos partidos ao TSE, e também a situação de cada um: se estão concorrendo ou inaptos para concorrer, conforme decisão da Justiça Eleitoral.

articles.standfirst: RN tem 153 candidatos na disputa por 24 vagas; votação será em 4 de outubro.
articles.summary: RN tem 153 candidatos na disputa por 24 vagas; votação será em 4 de outubro.
articles.body:
O Rio Grande do Norte (RN) tem 153 candidatos disputando 24 vagas na Assembleia Legislativa nas Eleições 2026, segundo dados do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE).

A votação será realizada em 4 de outubro, e as vagas são distribuídas entre partidos e federações pelo sistema proporcional, para mandatos de quatro anos.

A lista abaixo traz os nomes e os números de urna dos candidatos, enviados pelos partidos ao TSE, e também a situação de cada um: se estão concorrendo ou inaptos para concorrer, conforme decisão da Justiça Eleitoral.

articles.title: Festa do Peão de Ipaussu é cancelada por determinação da Justiça | G1
articles.standfirst: Evento com atrações do sertanejo estava previsto para ocorrer entre os dias 17 e 20 de setembro. Administração municipal afirmou em nota que respeita a decisão e acatará a ordem.
articles.summary: Com shows de Luan Pereira e Guilherme e Santiago, a Festa do Peão de Ipaussu foi cancelada pela prefeitura após determinação judicial sobre verbas municipais.
articles.body:
9ª Festa do Peão de Ipaussu teria nomes como Guilherme e Santiago, Luan Pereira e Léo & Raphael — Foto: Divulgação

A 9ª Festa do Peão de Ipaussu (SP), prevista para ocorrer entre os dias 17 e 20 de setembro, foi cancelada, segundo nota divulgada pela Prefeitura Municipal na segunda-feira (31).

O cancelamento da atração é em decorrência do cumprimento de uma determinação judicial que levou em consideração a forma de utilização dos recursos públicos para realização do evento.

Nomes como as duplas Guilherme e Santiago, Léo & Raphael e o cantor Luan Pereira estavam entre as atrações da festa.

Em nota, a prefeitura informou que, embora os preparativos estivessem em andamento, a administração municipal respeita as decisões judiciais e adotará todas as medidas necessárias para atender a ordem emitida. ( Veja abaixo a nota na íntegra ).

Confira abaixo os vídeos mais acessados no g1:

Nas redes sociais, o prefeito Luizão (PSD) afirmou que o cancelamento trata-se de uma questão política e que a oposição do seu governo "conseguiu que a festa fosse cancelada".

No vídeo publicado, ele afirma que foi feita "uma denúncia de dotação orçamentária de contingência" para que não ocorresse a festa. ( Veja abaixo o pronunciamento completo ) .

A Prefeitura Municipal de Ipaussu vem a público esclarecer os motivos que levaram ao cancelamento da 9ª Festa do Peão de Ipaussu.

A decisão decorreu de uma determinação judicial relacionada à dotação orçamentária utilizada para a realização do evento, especificamente a utilização de recursos vinculados à Reserva de Contingência.

É importante esclarecer que o cancelamento não ocorreu por falta de recursos financeiros, nem em razão de dificuldades ou falta de investimentos nas áreas da Saúde, Educação ou em qualquer outro setor da administração municipal.

A questão discutida judicialmente é de natureza orçamentária, relacionada à forma de previsão e utilização da dotação para a realização da festa.

Também é importante registrar que a mesma modalidade de utilização da Reserva de Contingência foi empregada pela administração municipal em 2023, em circunstâncias semelhantes, sem que, à época, tivesse ocorrido qualquer questionamento ou denúncia que impedisse a realização do evento.

A Administração Municipal respeita a decisão judicial e, diante dela, não há possibilidade jurídica de realização da 9ª Festa do Peão de Ipaussu. Dessa forma, o evento está definitivamente cancelado.

A Prefeitura lamenta profundamente a situação, especialmente pelos impactos para a população, comerciantes, trabalhadores, profissionais envolvidos e todos aqueles que aguardavam a realização da tradicional Festa do Peão.

Por fim, a Administração reafirma que continuará trabalhando normalmente em todas as áreas do município, mantendo os investimentos e serviços públicos essenciais e cumprindo rigorosamente as determinações legais e judiciais.

articles.title: Super Alvinho: menino com altas habilidades quer voltar à escola | G1
articles.standfirst: Aos 10 anos, Alvinho já acumula conquistas, prêmios e certificados. Ele aprendeu a ler aos 4 anos com um aplicativo, aprendeu inglês na internet e desenvolveu um aplicativo para Harvard.
articles.summary: Super Alvinho, menino com altas habilidades que viveu em abrigo, mobiliza rede de apoio para retomar os estudos e realizar o sonho de criar robôs.
articles.body:
O menino Álvaro Siqueira de Melo, que tem altas habilidades , e a mãe Priscila de Melo precisaram morar em um abrigo do município do Rio por conta de dificuldades financeiras enfrentadas durante o tratamento da mãe contra uma tuberculose.

Com a repercussão do caso depois de uma matéria do jornal O Globo, uma corrente de solidariedade se formou e a família conseguiu dinheiro para retornar para Cabo Frio, onde o Super Alvinho, como é conhecido, tem uma bolsa de estudos em uma escola particular.

Nesta terça-feira, Priscila informou nas redes sociais do menino que arrecadou pouco mais de R$ 36 mil com a campanha de vendas do livro dele e doações.

Super Alvinho e a mãe Priscila de Melo — Foto: Reprodução

Aos 10 anos, Alvinho já acumula conquistas, prêmios e certificados. Ele aprendeu a ler aos 4 anos com um aplicativo, aprendeu inglês na internet e desenvolveu um aplicativo para Harvard contando as dificuldades de um menino negro na comunidade.

"Esse aplicativo eu fiz para um curso de programação em Harvard, é de programação em blocos. O jogo fala sobre a minha história, foi feito em inglês e eu fiz com 7 anos. Também fala sobre o parquinho que vive quebrado nas comunidades, também fala sobre a escola pública que não tem atendimento especializado para crianças com altas habilidades", explica Alvinho.

Álvaro Siqueira de Melo, o Alvinho, em 2025 — Foto: Redes sociais

"Hoje eu quero ser um grande construtor de robôs na Europa. Tem um cowork em um shopping e lá é um espaço para estudos. Cada um chega e fica estudando ou trabalhando. A minha mãe está terminando o mestrado e eu tô pensando em voltar para a Legacy nesse ano e o meu sonho principal é ser um grande construtor de robôs na Europa", conclui.

"Graças às matérias que saíram recentemente muitas pessoas se mobilizaram e ficamos muito surpresos com a corrente de solidariedade para que ele volte para a escola, que a gente retome a nossa vida e com a esperança de um futuro melhor, um futuro organizado para que ele possa estudar, se desenvolver e alcançar os sonhos dele", destaca a mãe.

Álvaro Siqueira de Melo, o Alvinho, em 2023 — Foto: Redes sociais

Priscila aponta ainda as dificuldades de criar uma criança com altas habilidades sem apoio.

"É muito difícil, principalmente sendo mãe solo sem contar com nenhum benefício ou pensão, contando única exclusivamente com meu trabalho é um desafio. São muitos gastos, muitos desafios. Eu fiquei enferma e foi muito difícil proporcionar para ele tudo que ele precisa", afirma.

"Desejo que os sonhos dele tenham asas e possam voar mesmo, se realizar, que ele possa progredir e avançar. Quando eu descobri que ele tinha altas habilidades, tive medo de não ter condições de dar tudo que ele precisava para se desenvolver e realmente não é fácil, são muitos desafios", conclui.

🟩O g1 Rio está no GloboPop , o novo aplicativo de vídeos curtos verticais da Globo, disponível gratuitamente no seu celular. Lá no app, você pode seguir o palco do g1 Rio para não perder nenhum episódio. Baixe o GloboPop.

Essa não foi a primeira vez que ela teve dificuldades de manter o ensino dele . Em 2025, o RJ2 mostrou que ele não estava conseguindo acessar a escola no Jardim Botânico, Zona Sul do Rio, por falta de um transporte escolar.

Eram cerca de 20 quilômetros diários que Alvinho deveria cruzar para estudar em um instituto que atende jovens superdotados em situação de vulnerabilidade.

No ano anterior, o prefeito Eduardo Paes, em um evento com o presidente Lula, tinha prometido transporte escolar para o garoto. O serviço foi oferecido, mas no retorno escolar foi cortado.

“Alegaram que eles nem poderiam ter oferecido o transporte porque é exclusivo para pessoas com deficiências de locomoção. Mas a criança com altas habilidades tem o direito do atendimento de um educador especializado e, para ter acesso, é necessário transporte”, explicou Priscila na época.

Os votos serão para presidente, governador, senador, deputado federal e deputado estadual (ou distrital, apenas no caso do Distrito Federal). Todos os cargos têm mandato de quatro anos, exceto o de senador, cujo mandato é de oito anos.

O Senado vai renovar 54 das 81 cadeiras (dois terços do total). E cada eleitor deve votar em dois candidatos diferentes.

Na lista do TSE, os candidatos são classificados em duas situações principais: concorrendo ou inapto.

Cassado com recurso, indeferido com recurso ou pedido não conhecido com recurso;

Em algumas listas, o mesmo candidato aparece mais de uma vez. O TSE informa que manterá os nomes duplicados, mas apontará apenas uma das opções como apta ("concorrendo") até o dia da eleição.

articles.title: Wincobank baby death: Newborn died of stab wounds - police
articles.summary: A baby girl who was pronounced dead at a property in Sheffield was stabbed, police confirm.
articles.body:
A newborn baby girl who was discovered fatally injured at a house in Sheffield died as a result of stab wounds, police have said.

The baby was found at a house on Holywell Heights in the Wincobank area on Sunday morning, after police were called to reports of concern for her safety.

South Yorkshire Police said despite the best efforts of police and paramedics, the baby died at the scene.

Seven people aged between 15 and 37 were arrested on suspicion of her murder. Two of them, aged 26 and 37, were later bailed, but police confirmed on Tuesday a warrant had been obtained to extend time in custody for the remaining five as inquiries continued.

Det Ch Insp Tom Woodward, leading the investigation, said: "We recognise this is deeply distressing for those who would have loved to have a chance to love this baby girl, for the emergency services who responded and for the community who will inevitably be shocked by this incident.

"Everyone involved in responding to this tragedy - from the first officers and paramedics on the scene to the detectives now leading the investigation - has felt the profound impact of this investigation."

He added: "Our commitment to this little girl is unwavering. We will confront every difficult and distressing challenge and pursue every line of inquiry with determination and care to secure justice for her.

"We know the local community will hold her in their thoughts and support us as we work through this complex investigation."

A South Yorkshire Police spokesperson said officers were continuing their investigations in the Holywell Heights area and asked anyone with information that might be useful to contact them.

A neighbour told the BBC that a family moved into the house where the baby was found about eight months ago - a man, a woman and three teenagers.

According to the neighbour, they were quiet but had a lot of visitors, with large gatherings regularly held at the three-bedroom house, though there was little noise.

"We'd only hear the front door opening and closing, but they never gave us any concern," she said.

The neighbour said she had not heard any noise at the property before the arrival of the police on Sunday morning.

She said a chaotic scene ensued, with many police officers and a medic at the property.

She said she was not aware of any pregnant women living at the house and was confused when she found out a newborn baby had died at the address.

articles.title: Bedford school to admit girls for first time in its history
articles.summary: The school is making the change for the first time since it was founded in 1552.
articles.body:
A public school will admit girls for the first time since it was founded in 1552.

The Harpur Trust, which has managed Bedford School since 1764, said it would become co-educational from September 2027 as part of an investment it will make in its schools over the next 12 months.

Plans also include upgraded facilities at Bedford Girls' School, campus improvements at Bedford Modern School and expanded childcare funding at Pilgrims Pre-Preparatory School.

The trust said: "The investment will ensure that each school continues to offer an outstanding and distinctive educational experience into the future."

It added that changes to Bedford School, an independent day and boarding school, would make "education available to more young people, while enhancing the experience of those already part of the school community".

A new music centre and recital space will be developed at Bedford Girls' School, alongside investment in its sports programme and a new wellbeing hub.

Bedford Modern School will get a revamped reception area and multi-faith prayer room as part of an ongoing refurbishment programme.

Families with children at Pilgrims Pre-Preparatory School will also be able to access 30 hours of free childcare a week.

David Steadman, the trust's chief executive, said: "The world of education is changing rapidly, and we continually review how our schools can best meet the needs of current and future generations.

"We are confident that these plans will enable our schools to continue delivering an outstanding educational experience for generations to come."

articles.title: Meet Crown Princess Ingrid Alexandra: The 22-year-old Norway’s first adult heir as King Haakon takes oath, could become first reigning queen in over 600 years since Queen Margaret
articles.summary: Europe News: As Norway begins a new royal chapter, Crown Princess Ingrid Alexandra is stepping into the spotlight. At 22, she is the first new heir apparent in the.
articles.body: As Norway begins a new royal chapter, Crown Princess Ingrid Alexandra is stepping into the spotlight. At 22, she is the first new heir apparent in the country’s modern royal history to already be an adult when her parent becomes monarch.Her father, King Haakon VIII, took his Oath of Allegiance to the Norwegian Constitution before the Storting, the country’s parliament, on Tuesday, September 1. The ceremony came days after the death of his father, King Harald V, at the age of 89.Following Harald’s death on August 28, his son became king and his wife, Mette-Marit, became queen. Their eldest child, Ingrid Alexandra, is now crown princess and next in line to the throne.Who is Crown Princess Ingrid Alexandra?Born on January 21, 2004, Ingrid Alexandra is the eldest child of King Haakon and Queen Mette-Marit. She has grown up in the public eye while also pursuing an education outside the traditional royal setting.She recently began a new semester at the University of Oslo after transferring from the University of Sydney in Australia. She had been studying for a three-year bachelor’s degree focused on international relations and political economy before returning to Norway earlier this year.Her decision to return home came as her mother faced serious health challenges following a lung transplant in June.Why Ingrid Alexandra’s position is historicIngrid Alexandra’s accession to the role of heir marks an important change for the Norwegian monarchy. Previous heirs, including her father and grandfather, were under 18 when they became next in line following their fathers’ accession and had to take the required oath after reaching adulthood.She is also the first Norwegian royal heir whose position has been shaped entirely by the country’s 1990 succession reform. The change introduced absolute primogeniture, giving the throne to the monarch’s eldest child regardless of gender.That meant Ingrid Alexandra remained ahead of her younger brother, Prince Sverre Magnus, in the line of succession.King Haakon himself was born before the reform, which meant he inherited his position ahead of his elder sister, Princess Märtha Louise, under the succession rules that existed at the time.If Ingrid Alexandra eventually becomes monarch, she will be Norway’s first reigning queen in more than 600 years. The country’s last female head of state was Queen Margaret, who ruled from 1388 to 1412.Ingrid Alexandra is part of Europe’s new generation of royal heirsThe Norwegian crown princess is also part of a wider generation of young female heirs across Europe.She has a friendship with Princess Elisabeth of Belgium and Princess Catharina-Amalia of the Netherlands, who are both first in line to their respective thrones. The three royals have previously been reported to share a WhatsApp group chat.“We’ve known each other for a long time and see each other occasionally at events,” Princess Elisabeth said in a recent interview.“In my generation, there are several women. You see a similar shift in other monarchies,” she added. “We are all in the same situation. It’s a hurdle we will face together.”Queen Mette-Marit makes first official appearance after Harald’s deathWhile Haakon formally began his reign, the royal family continued mourning King Harald.On Monday, Queen Mette-Marit joined a solemn procession as her late father-in-law’s coffin was moved through the Royal Palace to the royal chapel. It marked her first official appearance since becoming queen.Mette-Marit walked alongside Queen Sonja, Harald’s widow, with the two women holding hands as they followed the coffin.The Queen has largely stayed away from public duties following her lung transplant in June. She was diagnosed with pulmonary fibrosis in 2018, a progressive condition that damages and scars lung tissue and can cause severe breathing difficulties.She was unable to attend Haakon’s swearing-in ceremony on Tuesday after experiencing complications related to her transplant.A pulmonologist from the National Hospital said in a statement that such complications can occur following a lung transplant and that Mette-Marit needed to be monitored throughout the day.King Harald’s funeral will be held on September 9King Harald’s coffin arrived at the Royal Palace in Oslo on Friday after his death and remained in the Red Salon over the weekend.On Monday, it was transferred to the royal chapel, where it will remain until the funeral. Members of the public will be able to visit the chapel and pay their respects to the late king from Tuesday, according to Norwegian broadcaster NRK.The royal family and the country are currently observing an official period of mourning. Over the weekend, Norwegians and visitors gathered outside the palace to leave flowers, cards and candles in memory of Harald.His state funeral is scheduled for September 9.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: More than 110 rescued a week after Nepal deadly floods, army says
articles.summary: More than 3,900 people remain missing after floodwaters surged across the Nepal-Tibet border last week.
articles.body:
One hundred and nineteen people have been rescued using air resources in Nepal following deadly floods, a spokesperson for the country's army said.

It comes nearly a week after the disaster that hit both Nepal and neighbouring Tibet, killing more than 1,000 people, with more than 3,900 still missing.

A Nepali army spokesperson earlier said a British male was among those rescued, along with 118 Nepalese people, of whom 44 were female and 74 male.

Later on Tuesday, the British man, Alastair Chambers, told the Telegraph and PA Media he was not rescued and had travelled to the region to help with aid efforts.

The BBC has contacted the UK Foreign Office for comment.

On Tuesday, Foreign Office minister Lord Wood of Anfield confirmed 36 British people remain unaccounted for - an increase from the 33 previously reported.

More than 600 are workers believed to be trapped in a vast network of mud-filled tunnels at hydropower sites along Trishuli River are among the thousands who are still missing.

Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah said on Monday that 279 people had been rescued from the sites.

The rescue operation is being spearheaded by an international team made up of Chinese and Nepalese military personnel, while experts from India, Korea and Australia are also involved.

On Tuesday, the Nepalese Tourist Board said it had rescued 330 foreign nationals in total.

Saturday saw a rapid development team from the UK arrive in Nepal to provide support for Britons and their families.

The team will work alongside the British embassy and local authorities to support British nationals arriving in and leaving Nepal in the coming days and weeks.

It comes after Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the UK had offered £5m to help the Nepalese government following the floods, saying it was a "very distressing and devastating situation".

He had previously urged Britons in the region "to follow guidance from the local authorities and follow our travel advice".

The flood hit early on Wednesday in Rasuwa, just north of Nepal's capital Kathmandu.

Preliminary information suggested it was caused by an earthquake, but the US Geological Survey said additional analysis indicated "the seismic energy was instead generated by a landslide".

It said a magnitude 5.2 seismic event caused by a "glacial collapse and debris flow" occurred near the border at 08:37 local time (03:52GMT) on Wednesday.

articles.title: 454-million-year-old supervolcano found beneath England may explain a vast ash layer across northern Europe
articles.summary: Rest of World News: More than 454 million years ago, a huge volcanic system erupted beneath what is now eastern England. Scientists have now found evidence of the long-ex.
articles.body: More than 454 million years ago, a huge volcanic system erupted beneath what is now eastern England. Scientists have now found evidence of the long-extinct volcano buried beneath The Wash, offering new clues about the region’s ancient past. Researchers from the British Geological Survey and the University of Oslo studied tiny crystals preserved in rock samples from boreholes in Norfolk and Lincolnshire. The crystals helped them date the eruption to about 454.4 million years ago. The findings also suggest that this ancient volcano may have produced the Kinnekulle ash layer, which is found across parts of Norway, Sweden, the Baltic region, Belarus and Poland. At the time, the land that would become England was separated from Scandinavia by the Tornquist Sea. Though the volcano disappeared millions of years ago, evidence of the eruption remained buried beneath the landscape.Ancient supervolcano beneath The Wash was once a vast volcanic complexThe ancient supervolcano was centred beneath The Wash, with its remains stretching into parts of Norfolk and Lincolnshire. Scientists identified evidence of the volcanic system in rock samples recovered from two boreholes about 65 kilometres apart. It was active during the Late Ordovician period, more than 450 million years ago, when the landscape and position of the continents were very different from today. The area that would later become England was then part of Avalonia and lay near an active zone of volcanic activity. Over millions of years, the volcano was buried beneath younger layers of rock and sediment. Scientists believe one of its eruptions sent several hundred cubic kilometres of material high into the atmosphere.Tiny zircon crystals revealed when the ancient eruption occurredThe evidence came from zircon crystals found in samples taken from boreholes at North Creake in Norfolk and Claxby in Lincolnshire. Zircon forms inside molten magma and can preserve a timestamp for the crystal because uranium within the mineral decays into lead. By analysing these isotopes, researchers dated crystals from both locations to 454.4 million years ago. That age closely matches dating obtained for the Kinnekulle tephra in the Oslo region. The researchers compared the chemistry of apatite crystals in the English samples with material from the ash layer. The similarities strengthen the proposed link between the buried volcanic complex and the tephra.Ancient eruption may explain the mysterious Kinnekulle ash layerThe eruption may explain the origin of the Kinnekulle tephra, a layer of altered volcanic ash preserved across Europe. The deposit occurs in parts of Norway, Sweden, the Baltic region, Belarus and Poland. The Tornquist Sea separated the land that became England from Scandinavia. Researchers propose that an eruption in eastern England sent ash high into the atmosphere, allowing the plume to cross the sea before material settled on the seafloor in Scandinavia. Chemical similarities between apatite crystals provide further evidence.Why the extinct supervolcano beneath England poses no modern threatIts remains are not visible as a volcanic mountain because geological processes have transformed and covered the landscape. The research reconstructs the volcano from minerals preserved in rocks recovered from boreholes. The findings show the value of geological archives, since the samples used in the analysis were collected decades ago and examined with modern techniques. Researchers say the work provides evidence linking the Kinnekulle tephra to eastern England. It offers a picture of volcanic activity that shaped the region during the Ordovician period.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Sudhikaran row: BJP SC Morcha performs ‘buddhi-shuddhi’ ritual for Rahul Gandhi
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: The political row over the alleged purification ritual at Haldwani's Ramlila Ground following Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's rally.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The political row over the alleged purification ritual at Haldwani's Ramlila Ground following Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's rally last month has intensified, with the BJP Scheduled Caste Morcha performing a ‘buddhi-shuddhi’ ritual for Congress leader Rahul Gandhi at Panchayati Temple in Dehradun.The development came as Uttarakhand Congress chief Ganesh Godiyal led a massive protest march towards the state Secretariat, condemning the alleged ‘purification’ ritual conducted after Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's August 8 rally in Haldwani.Accompanied by AICC co-in-charges Surendra Sharma and Manoj Yadav and hundreds of Congress workers, Godiyal attempted to gherao the Secretariat. Heavy police deployment was made to disperse the protesters, while several workers were detained as they raised slogans.The controversy centres on allegations that a ‘suddhikaran yajna’ was conducted at Haldwani's Ramlila Ground after Kharge's address. Congress leaders have criticised the alleged ritual, calling it an insult to the party president and an instance of caste discrimination."The rally happened in Haldwani, and then that place has a suddhikaran and havan. Then, the BJP State President justifies it and says that it is okay. What else could be more shameless?...BJP is working on the RSS agenda," Uttarakhand Assembly Leader of Opposition Yashpal Arya told ANI.The controversy also led to an FIR against Rahul Gandhi following a complaint by a member of the Scheduled Caste community, who alleged that the Congress leader's remarks about the purification ritual hurt the sentiments of the community.According to the complaint, members of the Valmiki community participated in cleaning the venue and conducting the ritual after the Congress rally attended by Kharge and other leaders.Godiyal, along with Surendra Sharma, Manoj Yadav and Congress workers, had also reached Dehradun's Kotwali Police Station on Monday seeking registration of an FIR against those responsible for the Haldwani incident.The row has since spread beyond Uttarakhand, with Congress units in several states protesting over the alleged ritual. Rahul Gandhi and AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi have also criticised the incident, describing it as a manifestation of a "Manuvadi mindset" and alleging that it was an attempt to demean a Dalit leader.The BJP has denied involvement in the ceremony. Union Minister and Leader of the House JP Nadda condemned the act in Parliament, saying the BJP had no association with the organisers and that the matter would be investigated.The organisers, Shri Ram Sena, along with local BJP representatives, maintained that the havan was not conducted because of Kharge's caste. They claimed the ritual was performed because religious decorum had allegedly been violated at the Ramlila Ground.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Destroyed desalination plant worsens Gaza’s drinking water crisis
articles.summary: After a newly built desalination plant was destroyed, displaced families in northern Gaza struggle to find clean water.
articles.body:
Gaza City, Gaza Strip – Zuhair al-Nasr walks through Gaza City’s Sheikh Radwan neighbourhood carrying two water containers, looking for somewhere to fill them.

The 74-year-old is not sure where he will find drinking water for his family.

For the past week, he says, he has barely been able to fill the containers. The water he has managed to get comes from a groundwater well rather than the desalinated water he used to rely on.

Only weeks ago, Zuhair did not have to search like this.

A newly built desalination plant near the tents where he lives had brought clean drinking water to his area. Pipes had been connected, allowing residents to access water around the clock.

For about two months, Zuhair says, the plant made managing life during Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza a little bit easier.

Zuhair lives with his large family – he has 13 children and more than 20 grandchildren – in a tent because his home in Beit Hanoon, north of Gaza City, was destroyed by Israel during the war.

Securing water for the family is a vital daily task, and the desalination plant meant that he no longer had to carry water over long distances.

But then, on August 24, Israel bombed the desalination plant , as it continues to flout the October ceasefire deal it agreed to.

The strike destroyed the plant and also damaged nearby displacement tents and residential structures.

Without the plant, Zuhair and Palestinians across Sheikh Radwan have been forced to go back to travelling long distances to get water.

“We were comfortable,” Zuhair says. “We’re suffering now. The water is the lifeline of our life. For drinking, cooking, washing and bathing.”

Zuhair says his neighbourhood had become cleaner and more lively after the desalination plant arrived earlier this year. A steady and reliable source of clean water had encouraged people to return and resettle the area.

“Where there is water, there is life,” he says.

For families who had already lost their homes and been displaced by the war, the plant offered a rare sense of stability.

But the relief lasted only about two months.

When residents received an Israeli forced evacuation order, Zuhair says, he hoped the desalination plant would not be the target.

Zuhair remains bewildered by its destruction. He points out that the facility was a civilian water station serving families in an area already facing a severe drinking-water shortage.

He rejects Israeli allegations that the site was being used for purposes other than supplying water, saying claims that it was next to a weapons storage facility were false.

“Why destroy a place that was providing people with water?” Zuhair asks.

A plant built for a thirsty neighbourhood

Mohammed Mahmoud, 53, the owner of the now-destroyed desalination plant, says the facility had been operating for only two months before it was attacked.

According to Mahmoud, it was the only desalination plant serving much of Sheikh Radwan and had been providing free desalinated water to 17 shelters and collective centres.

Mahmoud now estimates his losses at no less than $500,000. The desalination machinery and equipment alone cost about $250,000.

The plant had been built using equipment and materials that were already difficult and expensive to obtain during the war.

The destruction came as Gaza’s wider drinking-water crisis was already deepening.

A survey cited by the United Nations found that 90 percent of Gaza’s population was experiencing frequent and unpredictable disruptions in access to safe, clean and reliable water for drinking, cooking and hygiene in early July.

In Gaza City, the figure was even higher, at 92 percent.

About 75 percent of Gaza’s population continued to rely on water provided by trucks as their primary source of drinking water at the end of July, with humanitarian partners delivering more than 20,000 cubic metres a day to thousands of collection points.

Yet even that system is struggling to meet demand.

UNICEF reported in August that up to 63 percent of people were unable to collect the minimum six litres (1.5 gallons) of water per person per day recommended for drinking and cooking.

For families in northern Gaza, the disappearance of another local source means greater dependence on a system that is already struggling to reach them.

Nada Arouqi, a 36-year-old mother of four living in the Mukhabrat area in northwest Gaza City, says water trucks often only reach her neighbourhood two days a week.

Sometimes, she says, they do not come for an entire week.

Now, whenever a truck arrives, she has to make the most of it. “It has become an emergency situation,” she says.

She fills six containers and carries them from the collection point back to where her family lives.

There is no separate supply for bathing or cleaning, leaving the family dependent on the same water for drinking and other daily needs.

When the water does not come, she has to buy drinking water.

The shortage has also raised concerns about the cleanliness of the water that comes via the trucks.

Nada says one of her children developed a stomach illness and spent three or four days in hospital. She says doctors told her the illness was related to the water.

For a family already struggling to secure enough water, buying drinking water is another expense they can barely afford.

Her mother-in-law, 60-year-old Maryam Arouqi, who lives in the same displacement tent, describes another consequence of the shortage: the physical toll of bringing water home.

She says she has to refill a large household barrel three or four times a day because her family depends on it throughout the day.

There is no municipal water supply or household groundwater pump available to her, she says.

“I have to carry water,” Maryam says. “My body and bones are collapsing because of this.”

She describes tendon injuries, problems with her hands, chest pain and high blood pressure, and says she has been advised to stop the strenuous work.

But stopping is not an option when water is needed for an entire household. She and her grandchildren keep walking with empty containers, looking for somewhere to fill them.

“Our struggle for water never ends. Who can live without water? Water is life,” she says.

articles.title: 'Very justified': Trump says US striking Iran targets, warns of ‘harder’ attacks
articles.summary: US News: US President Donald Trump warned Iran of a much stronger American response if Tehran retaliates after the US military launched strikes on Iranian targ.
articles.body: US President Donald Trump warned Iran of a much stronger American response if Tehran retaliates after the US military launched strikes on Iranian targets near the Strait of Hormuz.In a post on Truth Social, Trump said the US was "as we speak, striking Iranian Targets near the Strait of Hormuz", describing the strikes as "large and powerful".Trump said the action was in retaliation for what he described as Iran's "failed attempt" to add sea mines to the Strait of Hormuz and the launch of eight missiles at a US military base in Jordan, which he said were all intercepted."The United States is, as we speak, striking Iranian Targets near the Strait of Hormuz. The strikes are large and powerful, and in retaliation for the Iranians’ failed attempt at adding sea mines to the Strait, which currently has no mines (They have been completely removed or detonated!), and the Iranians shooting eight missiles, all successfully knocked down, at our Military Base in Jordan. If the failed Nation of Iran retaliates for this very justified attack, they will be hit again at a much harder and higher level, but it will not be the biggest attack of them all, that is waiting in the wings and, when it is over, there will be very little left of the Islamic Republic of Iran."The warning came after the US military said it had begun striking Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targets in Iran at 1600 GMT on Tuesday.US Central Command (CENTCOM) said the strikes followed "recent attempted attacks" by the IRGC against commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and American service members deployed in the region.The latest strikes follow a US attack on Monday against two rocket launchers on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz. CENTCOM described the action as "limited, precise" and said the launchers were being prepared to "launch rockets and deploy sea mines into the Strait of Hormuz".Iran's IRGC said the attack killed two people and injured two others, and vowed "response and punishment".Iran subsequently said it had targeted US military bases in Jordan with ballistic missiles. Jordan's military said it intercepted eight missiles.Iranian state television also reported that Iranian forces targeted an air base in the UAE with drones. The UAE's Ministry of Defence rejected the report as "unfounded", while confirming that it had shot down a drone.Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said: "We are not seeking war, but we will deliver a decisive response to the aggressors."The escalation has centred on the Strait of Hormuz, a critical global shipping route between Iran and Gulf countries. The waterway is about 33 km wide at its narrowest point and has emerged as a major flashpoint in the ongoing conflict.CENTCOM also rejected an earlier IRGC claim that a supertanker had struck sea mines and caught fire while attempting to cross the strait through a route not authorised by Iran."This is yet another IRGC attempt to intimidate regional commercial shipping through disinformation," CENTCOM said.Trump has separately claimed that mines placed by Iran in the Strait of Hormuz have been removed or detonated, warning that any vessel deploying new mines would be destroyed. Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi dismissed the claim as a "propaganda" deception.The latest US action marks the first known American attack on Iran since Trump paused a renewed military campaign in late July, further escalating tensions around the strategically important waterway.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Maharashtra puts FDA action against loose edible oil sales on hold for 1 year
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis on Tuesday said enforcement action against the sale of loose edible oil would be kept in abeyance.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis on Tuesday said enforcement action against the sale of loose edible oil would be kept in abeyance for a year, putting the Food and Drug Administration’s (FDA) decision on hold.However, there would be no further extension after this period and compliance with the law would be mandatory, news agency PTI reported.Therefore, during this one-year period, every trader will have to make the necessary changes to their business practices in accordance with the law, Fadnavis said.Govt to form committees to help traders complyA joint committee comprising FDA representatives and traders will be constituted to recommend measures and provide guidance for implementing these changes, an official release said.The committee will recommend solutions and measures to help traditional traders understand what changes they need to make to comply with the law, it said.Fadnavis assured loose edible oil traders that the state government would provide assistance, facilities and, where necessary, grants or subsidies to help them make the transition.The committee will prepare a plan for legally compliant changes for traders, edible oil sellers, manufacturers and repackaging businesses involved in the sector.The government will endeavour to assist traders in creating quality-testing systems, packaging facilities and other necessary infrastructure, Fadnavis said.Earlier in the day, the CM chaired a meeting of loose edible oil traders at Mantralaya.Deputy CM Sunetra Pawar, revenue minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule, FDA and special assistance minister Narhari Zirwal and senior officials were present.“Enforcement action against the sale of loose edible oil would be kept in abeyance for one year for the time being. However, there would be no further extension after this period, and compliance with the law would be mandatory,” Fadnavis said.‘Need to balance law with needs of citizens’The CM said that there is a demand for and a need for loose edible oil even in rural areas. At the same time, the livelihoods of many traders depend on this business.Therefore, it is necessary to find an appropriate balance between the law and the needs of ordinary citizens.The use and sale of loose edible oil has been carried out traditionally in the state for many years. Hence, traders need to be given some time to change this system, the CM said.“The law will take its course; however, a transition period is necessary to move from traditional business practices to a system that complies with the law,” Fadnavis said.Two committees will be constituted to recommend solutions to issues related to the loose edible oil business.One of these committees will study the difficulties faced by traders operating through traditional methods and recommend measures required to help them make legally compliant changes.The second committee will recommend measures for creating the necessary arrangements and facilities for edible oil sellers, manufacturers, repackaging businesses and other stakeholders.Fadnavis directed both committees to coordinate and consult with all stakeholders and submit their reports to the government within one month.“The government does not wish to deprive any trader of their livelihood. While ensuring compliance with the law, emphasis will be placed on creating the necessary facilities so that traders can conduct their businesses in a better and safer manner. Wherever necessary, the government will extend its cooperation to help businesses adopt these changes,” Fadnavis said.FDA had warned against loose edible oilLast month, FDA commissioner Tukaram Mundhe had urged consumers not to buy loose or unsealed edible oil, calling it unsafe.He had said a compliance order had been issued for the sector due to violations, including adulteration.Following the FDA’s move, Fadnavis had stressed that the state government was seeking a “middle path” to balance strict quality enforcement with the livelihoods of traditional oil vendors and small consumers, PTI reported.Legal provisions introduced in 2011In addition to curbing adulteration of edible oil, the Centre had introduced legal provisions in this regard in 2011, taking into consideration its impact on citizens’ health.The Central Advisory Committee has issued directions for stricter regulation of the sale of loose edible oil.Four notifications have been issued for regulating the implementation of this law, up to August 28, 2020.There are currently 2,103 licensed loose edible oil businesses operating in the state.Of these, 370 businesses hold licences to sell edible oil after repackaging, while 489 businesses hold licences for edible oil production.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: Operation ‘Rotten Apple’: US arrests over 2,100 illegal immigrants across New York
articles.summary: US News: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) arrested 2,197 illegal immigrants in New York during a month-long operation, the Department of Homeland S.
articles.body: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) arrested 2,197 illegal immigrants in New York during a month-long operation, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) said on Tuesday.Operation Rotten Apple was conducted across New York state from July 27 to August 29. DHS said those arrested included individuals with criminal records involving murder, rape, kidnapping, drug trafficking and assault.US Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said the operation had helped make New York safer while accusing state and city officials of failing to cooperate with federal immigration authorities.“Over the course of this operation, we arrested murderers, rapists, pedophiles, drug traffickers, and violent assailants,” Mullin said at a press conference in New York City.DHS said several of those arrested had serious criminal records. They included Bogdan Detrovich Gren from Ukraine, who has convictions for kidnapping resulting in death, weapons possession and murder.Other arrests included Andreas Bernal Chiquito from Colombia, who had been arrested in cases involving sexual conduct with a child, and Noel Celestino Lopez Martinez from Mexico, who had been arrested on a first-degree rape charge.The department also identified Palvinder Singh from India, who it said had a rape conviction in Germany, and Carlos Mendez-Acosta from Venezuela, who had a rape conviction.DHS said people from Cambodia, the Dominican Republic, Sierra Leone, Honduras and Vietnam were also among those arrested. Their criminal records included allegations or convictions related to drug trafficking, heroin distribution, burglary, assault, drug possession and theft.Border czar Tom Homan also praised the operation and criticised New York's sanctuary policies, saying they prevent local authorities from cooperating with federal immigration officers.ICE officials said the operation focused on individuals considered public safety threats and that federal immigration laws would continue to be enforced across New York.DHS also accused New York Governor Kathy Hochul and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani of backing policies that limit cooperation with ICE.The department claimed that 13,621 criminal illegal immigrants had been released from New York jails because of these policies. However, DHS did not provide a detailed breakdown supporting that figure in its press release.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: US launches strikes on Iran following 'attempted attacks in Strait'
articles.summary: US Central Command accused Iran of targeting commercial shipping and American service members deployed in the region.
articles.body:
American forces resumed strikes against Iran on Tuesday, US Central Command has said in a statement.

It accused the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) of "recent attempted attacks" against commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and "American service members deployed to the region".

State media reported that a strike near Sirik in southern Iran had killed four people, including a four-year-old child, and wounded 50 at a wedding party.

The IRGC said the US would regret the strikes, and Iranian news agencies reported that retaliatory missile and drone attacks on "US bases and interests in the region" had begun.

Donald Trump, when the US strikes were announced, warned that Iran would be hit again at "a much harder and higher level" if it retaliated.

The attack follows the first known US strikes on Iran since late July earlier this week, when forces attacked two rocket launchers on Larak Island in the Strait. Tehran retaliated by firing missiles at air bases in Jordan and a drone at the UAE.

On Tuesday Centcom said US forces had begun striking IRGC targets at 12:00 ET (16:00 GMT).

As well as the Sirik strike, other reports said projectiles had hit the areas of Chabahar and Konarak and an airport in Jiroft, and that explosions were heard in Qeshm island and Bandar Abbas.

The IRGC was reported as saying it had launched a barrage of ballistic missiles at a US Marine base in Jordan's Aqaba in retaliation for the Sirik attack.

Jordan's state-affiliated Al-Mamlaka network reported that the country's national security centre had warned residents of the Aqaba and Mafraq governates of falling debris, adding that the warning had since ended.

Trump said Tuesday's "large and powerful" strikes were a response to Iran's targeting of a US military base in Jordan, adding the country had "failed" at adding sea mines to the Strait.

He also threatened that a much larger-scale attack was "waiting in the wings".

The US and Israel launched wide-ranging strikes on Iran on 28 February, with Iran responding by attacking Israel, US bases and allied states in the Gulf, and effectively closing the Strait of Hormuz to marine traffic.

A US-Iran agreement, known as the Memorandum of Understanding, to extend a ceasefire between the two countries was signed in June.

However that agreement has expired, leading to a resumption of hostilities. Both the US and Iran have also fired on shipping, with Tehran targeting vessels it says have sought to cross the Strait without its permission and the US enforcing a naval blockade of Iranian ports.

Washington also announced a fresh sanctions campaign on 24 August aimed at further isolating Tehran and expanding secondary sanctions against its allies.

Iranian officials and state media have largely dismissed the campaign as a continuation of previous US economic measures, which they argue followed Washington's military failure in the recent conflict.

However on Tuesday Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian was quoted by state media as saying if the US returned to committing to the agreement, Iran would reciprocate.

articles.title: How a small island in Canada appeared, vanished, and was found again
articles.summary: Officials in British Columbia say the floating island drifted towards the shoreline of a local lake. But its origins remain a mystery.
articles.body:
A small, floating island on a lake in the Canadian province of British Columbia has been spotted again after officials lost track of it on satellite images following its initial discovery.

The forested island was first spotted in the middle of Williston Reservoir, BC's largest fresh water lake, in early August by boaters who captured the scene in a video that has since gone viral.

A satellite image from late July confirmed the existence of the island, which is the size of about one-and-a-half American football fields. But a few weeks later, it had vanished from that spot.

Officials in BC say they have now been able to locate it again near shore, though it's unclear where it came from.

Bob Gammer, a spokesperson for BC Hydro, a government-owned utility that maintains the reservoir and a nearby dam, first learned of the island's existence after seeing a video of it circulating on Canadian social media pages.

The video, taken by boaters, shows a forested patch of land that appeared to be bobbing in the water.

Gammer said he at first thought it was an AI-generated clip.

"I thought, well, this could be anywhere," he told the BBC. "Maybe it's not real."

But a satellite image pulled up by his team from 21 July confirmed it was real, and was indeed floating in the middle of the reservoir in a remote northern part of the province.

The island, however, appeared to have vanished in a satellite image taken just a few weeks later on 5 August. Its disappearance was covered by several international news outlets, sparking intrigue around the globe.

"We just don't know where it went," Gammer said. "Did it sink? Did it find its way into another corner of the reservoir?"

Gammer said he can now put the questions to bed. The island, he said, appears to have simply drifted towards shore and landed around 30 km (18.6 miles) from where it was first spotted.

This was confirmed by a new satellite image and a couple of eyewitness accounts from pilots flying above, he said.

BC Hydro estimates the island to be 9,800 square metres, or one hectare - roughly the size of one Canadian football field, or 1.5 American football fields.

As to its origins, Gammer said BC Hydro is still not entirely sure, but there is one strong theory: the island likely formed over many years from accumulating driftwood that served as a base for plants and trees to take root.

He added he believes it broke off from the reservoir's shoreline this summer as water levels rose to a high not seen since 2012.

Floating islands have been spotted elsewhere.

One such island in Wisconsin's Lake Chippewa is known as the Forty Acre Bog. It is thought to be the result of peat bogs detaching from the bottom of the lake and floating to the surface.

Some years, local boaters will push the floating bog to prevent it from drifting towards a local bridge.

It houses diverse wildlife, according to the Lake Chippewa Flowage Resort Association, such as frogs and salamanders, and - like the rest of the lake and its shoreline - is legally protected by state laws.

Local resident Cheryl Treland told Wisconsin Public Radio in 2024 that the bog is "like an iceberg".

"This isn't like a leaf floating on the top of the water," she said.

Gammer cautioned that the island in BC is not a stable structure, and he advised against attempting to step foot on it.

"It is remote, and most people will never come near it," he said.

For those with the means and the drive to seek it out, he had this warning: "Stay off the island. It could break apart."

articles.title: US embassies in Middle East warn Americans of 'unforeseen escalation' as latest strikes hit Iran
articles.summary: Multiple U.S. embassies warned Americans in the Middle East to "exercise caution and heightened vigilance," while CENTCOM launched fresh strikes on Iran.
articles.body: Multiple U.S. embassies in the Middle East warned Americans Tuesday of the "potential for unforeseen escalation" as U.S. Central Command launched fresh strikes on Iran. Similar messages posted on the websites of the U.S. embassies in Jerusalem, Jordan and Qatar said, "Americans currently in the Middle East should exercise caution and heightened vigilance and should be prepared for flight cancellations, periodic airspace closures, and potential travel disruptions." The warnings came as CENTCOM said its forces "began striking Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targets in Iran" around 12 p.m. ET. "The strikes follow recent attempted attacks by the IRGC against commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and against American service members deployed to the region," CENTCOM added. US STRIKES IRGC, IRANIAN PORT TARGETS AFTER TRUMP VOWS TO 'HIT BACK HARD' "The strikes are large and powerful, and in retaliation for the Iranians’ failed attempt at adding sea mines to the Strait, which currently has no mines (They have been completely removed or detonated!), and the Iranians shooting eight missiles, all successfully knocked down, at our Military Base in Jordan," Trump wrote on Truth Social on Tuesday. "If the failed Nation of Iran retaliates for this very justified attack, they will be hit again at a much harder and higher level, but it will not be the biggest attack of them all, that is waiting in the wings and, when it is over, there will be very little left of the Islamic Republic of Iran!" he added. U.S. strikes over the weekend targeted two Iranian rocket launchers on an island in the Strait of Hormuz, the first such strikes in a month. Iranian forces were preparing to launch rockets carrying sea mines into the strait when U.S. forces targeted Larak Island, U.S. Central Command said. In response, Iran launched eight ballistic missiles targeting U.S. bases in Jordan. NEW REPORT EXPOSES INTACT IRANIAN BUNKER THAT MAY HIDE REGIME'S ONGOING NUCLEAR WORK The embassies also said Tuesday, "Due to tensions in the Middle East, the security environment remains complex with the potential for unforeseen escalation. "U.S. diplomatic facilities, including outside the Middle East, have been targeted. Iran and groups supportive of Iran may target other U.S. interests overseas or at locations associated with the United States and Americans throughout the world, including U.S. businesses and other institutions," it continued. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "The situation in the Middle East remains fluid," the message also said. "The Iranian regime is unpredictable, as seen by its recent decisions to attack areas in the region without warning or provocations as well as to expand attacks to areas not previously targeted (such as Egypt). Americans should remain vigilant, as merely because U.S. interests or businesses have not been attacked in a country in the past does not ensure their safety." articles.title: This Montana family ranch was valued at $3.5 million; the owners gave up $2.9 million in development value to protect it
articles.summary: US News: In Montana's Paradise Valley, just north of Yellowstone National Park, the Nickelson family has permanently protected 437 acres of working ranchland f.
articles.body: In Montana's Paradise Valley, just north of Yellowstone National Park, the Nickelson family has permanently protected 437 acres of working ranchland from subdivision and development while retaining ownership of the property. On March 13, 2026, the Gallatin Valley Land Trust completed a conservation easement on the ranch, a legal agreement that permanently restricts future development while allowing the property to remain in private hands and continue to support agricultural use. The ranch was appraised at $2.3 million in 2023 and more recently at $3.5 million, with the conservation easement resulting in a donated conservation value of $2.9 million. Rather than selling the property or transferring it to a public agency, the Nickelson family chose to give up that portion of the property's potential value in exchange for permanent protection. The decision preserves a working landscape in one of Montana's most rapidly changing valleys while allowing the ranch to remain part of the family's legacy.How a conservation easement lets a family keep ranching while blocking developmentAccording to Atira Conservation, which provided $25,000 in philanthropic support toward the conservation project, the Nickelson Ranch will remain privately owned while the Gallatin Valley Land Trust holds the permanent conservation easement. The arrangement separates ownership of the land from the development rights protected by the easement. The family can therefore retain the property and continue agricultural activities while the easement permanently limits subdivision and development, including for future owners. The ranch is currently leased to a neighbouring producer and remains an active agricultural property rather than becoming a publicly owned preserve. About 71% of the ranch consists of native rangeland, while another 26% is irrigated hay ground on prime soils. Protecting those agricultural areas preserves not only open space but also land that continues to contribute to the working landscape of Paradise Valley. The conservation easement therefore allows the property to remain economically useful as a ranch while preventing its future conversion into a collection of residential lots.Why this stretch of the Mill Creek drainage matters for migrating wildlifeThe Nickelson Ranch sits within the Mill Creek drainage, an important landscape for wildlife moving between the Absaroka-Beartooth Wilderness and the Upper Yellowstone River. According to Atira Conservation, the area provides critical winter range and a migratory corridor for species including elk, mule deer and white-tailed deer. Those seasonal movements depend on connected stretches of undeveloped land, making individual ranches important pieces of a much larger habitat network. Conservation easements can play a particular role in this landscape because they allow working ranches to remain privately owned while preventing the subdivision that can fragment open habitat. The Nickelson property therefore protects more than the acreage within its boundaries. Its location within the Mill Creek drainage means that keeping the land intact contributes to maintaining connectivity between larger natural areas and the river valley. In a region where residential growth and rising land values are placing increasing pressure on large ranch properties, permanently protecting individual parcels can help preserve the continuous landscapes wildlife use to move between seasonal habitats.How the Nickelson Ranch fits into a much larger conservation effort in Paradise ValleyThe Nickelson Ranch is part of a broader conservation effort taking place across Paradise Valley. According to Atira Conservation, the property contributes to a block of more than 5,000 acres of conserved and prospective lands within the Mill Creek drainage. It also adds to the work of the Gallatin Valley Land Trust's Northern Yellowstone Open Lands Initiative, through which approximately 12,000 acres in Paradise Valley have been protected over the past two years. The Nickelson property is directly adjacent to the recently conserved Warfield Ranch, creating an additional connection between protected working lands in the valley. The Warfield property also connects to land managed by the U.S. Forest Service, extending the conservation network beyond individual private ranches. Together, these projects demonstrate how conservation easements can protect large areas without requiring landowners to surrender ownership. For the Nickelson family, the decision meant accepting a lower development value for the ranch in exchange for ensuring that its future use would remain compatible with agriculture and conservation. The $2.9 million conservation contribution represents a substantial portion of the property's value, but it also permanently removes the possibility of subdivision that could otherwise transform the ranch's character. In a valley where open ranchland provides both agricultural value and wildlife connectivity, the easement ensures that the Nickelson Ranch will remain part of that landscape regardless of who owns it in the future.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Meera Syal reveals ‘older Asian actor’ in London tried to rape her in her 20s
articles.summary: UK News: LONDON: British Indian actor and screenwriter Meera Syal, famed for writing “Bhaji on the Beach” and co-writing and starring in the British Asian TV c.
articles.body: LONDON: British Indian actor and screenwriter Meera Syal, famed for writing “Bhaji on the Beach” and co-writing and starring in the British Asian TV comedy “Goodness Gracious Me”, has revealed that an older Asian actor had tried to rape her, when she was in her 20s, in London.The 65-year-old, made a dame in the 2026 New Year Honours list, told the Sunday Times that back in the 1980s, when she was struggling to find acting work and was singing in a jazz band in Covent Garden, applying for waitressing jobs, about to give up and go back to the West Midlands, an Asian actor she knew invited her “to a gathering” at his house in London, saying he was friends with casting directors. When she arrived, there was just one person, a musician, who swiftly left, leaving her alone with the unnamed older Asian man. She stayed for dinner, feeling it would be impolite not to do so, and after dinner, mid-conversation he “pounced on her and tried to rape her”.Then he tried to make small talk but she left and took a cab to her friend’s place, where she was staying, and did not tell anyone what happened, she said. She did not report it to police as it was the 1980s and the thought of putting her Punjabi parents, who had moved to the UK from Delhi, through a criminal trial was too much. “This is the first time I’ve spoken about this publicly,” she said ahead of her memoir “Vigilauntie: A Memoir — Innit?” being released in India. The book also delves into her Hindu and Sikh parents’ lives in India and Partition.The assault inspired the strong female characters she created in “Goodness Gracious Me”, a 1990s comedy that poked fun at British Indians and at British society, spurring “a real embracing of multicultural Britain”. “How times have changed,” she said. “It feels like we are back in the Seventies.”Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
