articles.title: Week one upset special: These three college football teams should be on upset alert this weekend
articles.summary: Auburn, UNLV and Clemson face serious upset potential in week one as new coaches, travel woes and locker room distractions cloud the favorites.
articles.body: I hope you all canceled your plans for the next 20 or so Saturdays, because college football is back. After a nice appetizer over the weekend courtesy of week zero, the action ramps up in earnest with a full slate of games going all the way through Labor Day. There are quite a few high-profile match ups on the docket for week one, and with that comes the inevitability of upsets. SEC LAWYERS, LANE KIFFIN AND DEATH VALLEY: COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S WEEK 1 IS SET FOR FIREWORKS It is college football, after all, and no season opener would be complete without a few shockers (happy 19th anniversary to Appalachian State's win at The Big House, by the way). With that in mind, here are three teams favored to win this weekend that should be on upset alert. Auburn Tigers (-7.5) vs. Baylor Bears Let me preface this pick by saying that I truly believe Auburn head coach Alex Golesh will do great things on The Plains, but this game reeks of upset potential. The Tigers are breaking in a ton of new players as well as the aforementioned new coaching staff, and the fact that this is at a neutral site in Atlanta makes this game extra wonky. The Baylor Bears weren't exactly world beaters last year, and new quarterback DJ Lagway was a train wreck at Florida in 2025, but he was dealing with a litany of injuries all last season as well as having to perform in a Billy Napier offense, so I expect the junior signal caller to look more like a five-star than he did throughout much of his time in Gainesville. SLEEPER TEAMS FROM EACH POWER 4 CONFERENCE: WHO WILL EXCEED EXPECTATIONS THIS COLLEGE FOOTBALL SEASON? Auburn won this game handily last year, too, but did so with an entirely different coaching staff and set of players, so that result is a largely irrelevant data point. I wouldn't put money on the Bears to win this game outright, but I wouldn't be shocked if they did, and I almost expect them to get inside that 7.5 number as Golesh tries to work through some first-game jitters. UNLV Rebels (-3) vs. Hawaii Rainbow Warriors If you had asked me to pick this game seven days ago, I would have hammered UNLV, but with the benefit of seeing both teams perform during week zero, I might have to pivot to the Rainbow Warriors of Hawaii. The Rebels struggled to stop Memphis's offense in the 27-21 loss to the Tigers at home, and I have a feeling some of that defensive fog lingers for this game too. Conversely, Hawaii might have actually gained some confidence in their week zero loss to Stanford, a game in which they were the underdogs and were leading midway through the fourth quarter. The biggest factor here is that the game is in Honolulu, and that kind of trans-Pacific travel coupled with a season-opening loss could spell trouble for the Rebels. If that does happen, and UNLV goes from G6 Playoff darlings to 0-2, some uncomfortable conversations will start to spring up about head coach Dan Mullen's future in Vegas. And no number of Elvis impersonators will be able to save him from that. Clemson Tigers vs. [11] LSU Tigers (-10) A good old-fashioned Tiger on Tiger match up, and this one has some layers to it, so bare with me. When these two teams met last year in South Carolina, it was thought to be somewhat of a College Football Playoff preview, with both LSU and Clemson ranked in the top-ten to start the season. As it turned out, both teams wound up winning only seven games apiece and LSU even sent head coach Brian Kelly packing. Now, the Bayou Bengals have Lane Kiffin roaming their sidelines armed with a $40 million roster, but there have been several distractions to come out of Baton Rouge in recent weeks, most notably the staff being at the center of the controversy regarding NFL players going back to college. That could prove to be enough of a headache for the coaches and players to make what should have been a fairly comfortable win into a dog fight, but that's not to say Clemson can't win this game even on their own merits. The talent disparity between the two teams isn't as wide as some say it is, and Clemson has some serious firepower at the wide receiver position as well as along its front seven. I do worry about how Clemson starting quarterback Christopher Vizzina will handle the noise in Death Valley with this being only his second career start, but he has the talent profile as well as the aforementioned stable of receivers to get the job done. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP LSU can ill afford to overlook this game, even as double-digit favorites, and no one should be shocked if Clemson comes in and plants their flag in Tiger Stadium.

articles.title: In 2008, Allen University paid $116,000 to move a historic 1903 house two blocks and promised restoration; 18 years later, the work never came and the house is being demolished
articles.summary: US News: A historic house in Columbia, South Carolina, that was once linked to generations of Black community and civil rights leaders is now being demolished .
articles.body: A historic house in Columbia, South Carolina, that was once linked to generations of Black community and civil rights leaders is now being demolished after years of efforts to save it failed, AOL reported.The Robert Weston Mance House was built in 1903 and was moved two blocks in 2008 by Allen University to make room for new student dormitories. The university had promised to restore the house after moving it, but the restoration never happened.Nearly two decades later, the two-storey American Foursquare house on Heidt Street has deteriorated badly. The city has formally declared it an unsafe structure, and demolition work has now begun.The demolition follows a long legal dispute between Allen University and the city over whether the house should be torn down. The university had argued that restoring the property would be too expensive, while preservation officials said the building was still structurally sound enough to save.Links to Columbia’s Black historyThe house became known as the Mance House after Rev. Robert Weston Mance bought it in 1922 while serving as president of Allen University. He lived there with his family, including his son, Dr Robert Weston Mance Jr.Mance Jr later became a physician and educator and served as superintendent of Waverly Hospital. The hospital was part of a wider Black community in Waverly, where African American residents built businesses and institutions during segregation.The neighbourhood included the Waverly Five & Dime, which was run by George Elmore. Elmore was among the men who successfully sued for the right of Black South Carolinians to vote in primary elections.Waverly Hospital was founded by African American doctor Norman A. Jenkins to provide medical care to Columbia’s Black community during segregation. The hospital later became part of Good Samaritan-Waverly Hospital.Allen University and Benedict College also became important institutions in the community. The Waverly Historic District was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1989 and became part of the National Park Service’s African American Civil Rights Network in 2021.University promised to restore houseThe Mance House originally stood at the corner of Pine and Hampton streets. In 2008, Allen University was carrying out an $18 million dormitory expansion and needed the property moved.The house was relocated to 1421 Heidt St, around half a mile from the university’s core. As part of the arrangement, the university agreed to restore the building to a liveable condition so that future university presidents could live there.The restoration promise was also linked to a financial guarantee from the federal Department of Education for the dormitory project and the relocation effort.At the time, then-university president Charles Young said, “The Mance House has been an important part of Allen’s history, and we are proud we have been able to save it.”But after the move, the promised restoration did not happen. The house remained empty. Before being relocated, it had been used for storage and office space.Over the years, its windows were broken, paint began to chip and code violations accumulated. By the time demolition became a serious issue, the building had been left vacant for years.Historic Waverly neighbourhood association president Ronald Davis said he understood the importance of the house but was concerned about its condition and safety.“I understand the significance of the building and how important it is, and history is important, but safety is my top priority as president of Historic Waverly, and I will not waver on that in any way,” Davis told The State.Davis said he had seen college students and homeless people entering the property. He also said he feared the roof could collapse or someone could start a fire.“Allen University had an opportunity to prevent the house from reaching that point. They did absolutely nothing to fix that building,” he said.Demolition attempt and court battleThe dispute came into the open in 2023, about 15 years after the house was moved. Neighbours saw a wrecking crew at the property and part of the roof had already been removed.However, no demolition permit had been issued. Allen University was ordered to stop the work and seek formal approval from the city.In February 2023, the city’s Design/Development Review Commission rejected the university’s request for a demolition permit.City preservation staff said the house had suffered damage because of years of neglect, but they did not consider it beyond repair. After visiting the property, staff wrote that it “appeared to be structurally sound” and was not in as serious a state of disrepair as many other historic buildings.Allen representatives told the commission that restoring the property would be expensive. One firm estimated that the work would cost more than $500,000.Eric Gamble, who was Allen’s vice president of planning and information technology at the time, told the commission that the university had to make decisions based on its own needs.“Allen University isn’t in the Waverly district to hurt it, but we have to make decisions that are applicable to the university,” Gamble said.He also told the board that Allen’s CEO and board of trustees had voted to demolish the property.The commission voted 4-1 against the demolition permit. Allen University then sued over the decision, and the dispute remained in court for more than two years before the parties agreed to dismiss the case.The city eventually approved a demolition permit this summer, allowing the university to proceed with taking down the house.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: In 1905, a Bohemian prince released five muskrats into his estate ponds as a fur venture. Within a decade, around 2 million were in Bohemia
articles.summary: Rest of World News: A small group of muskrats arrived in Bohemia in 1905, carried across the Atlantic as curiosities from a hunting trip in North America. Five animals we.
articles.body: A small group of muskrats arrived in Bohemia in 1905, carried across the Atlantic as curiosities from a hunting trip in North America. Five animals were released into ponds at Prince Colloredo-Mannsfeld’s estate near Dobříš, where they were expected to remain little more than a private collection and perhaps a source of valuable fur. They had other plans. Within years, the animals had moved beyond the estate and into the surrounding waterways, breeding as they went.By 1914, estimates put the muskrat population in Bohemia at around two million. From there, the animals continued their slow spread through rivers, canals and wetlands, reaching neighbouring countries and, through later introductions and escapes, much farther east. More than a century later, the descendants of those early European muskrats are found across a vast stretch of the continent, while countries such as the Netherlands still trap them to protect vulnerable waterways and embankments.Five muskrats released in Bohemia began an unexpected European spreadThis is generally traced to 1905, when Prince Colloredo-Mannsfeld returned to Bohemia after a hunting trip in North America, commonly described as having taken place in Alaska.According to the UNL Digital Commons (University of Nebraska), among the animals brought back were five muskrats: two males and three females. They were released into ponds at his estate near Dobříš, roughly 40 kilometres south-west of Prague.The intention appears to have been practical rather than scientific. Muskrat fur had commercial value, and keeping the animals on the estate offered the possibility of developing a small source of income. For a while, the newcomers were reportedly treated much like captive animals, receiving food such as grain and carrots.Muskrats are well suited to moving through connected waterways. Once animals began leaving the estate, streams and rivers provided a ready-made route into unfamiliar territory. Young muskrats also disperse from established populations, meaning the species did not need people to carry every new group farther afield.Within less than a decade, the situation looked very different. By 1914, estimates placed the muskrat population in Bohemia at around two million animals. The species had moved far beyond the ponds where those original five had been released.How the muskrat gradually expanded from Bohemia to JapanHistorical records from Europe allowed naturalists and later ecologists to follow the changing boundary of the muskrat's range. During the early decades, the advancing population front was estimated at roughly 10 kilometres a year, although movement was not uniform. Rivers and other waterways could provide much easier routes than areas without suitable habitat. At that pace, the animal was hardly racing across the continent. It was spreading in increments, generation after generation.Bohemia was followed by neighbouring parts of Central Europe. Muskrats reached Germany, Austria and Switzerland, while separate introductions and escapes helped establish populations elsewhere, including France and Belgium.The species was also deliberately moved for fur production. During the 1920s, muskrats were introduced into Finland, while much larger programmes followed in the Soviet Union from 1928 onwards. Animals were released in different regions, helping the species leap far beyond the original European population and eventually establish itself across parts of Siberia and Central Asia.From there came further expansion into China and Mongolia, with naturalised populations eventually reaching Japan as well.Rivers and canals helped the muskrat spread one waterway at a timeMuskrats do not need to travel great distances in a single burst to colonise new territory. The animals spend much of their lives around water and are capable swimmers. They excavate burrows into banks and build nests or lodges among vegetation. When populations become established, younger animals can disperse into neighbouring stretches of suitable habitat.That makes a river system rather different from a simple map of open land. A population established beside one stream can gradually occupy another stretch of water, then another. Given enough time, connected rivers, canals and wetlands can turn what looks like a local introduction into a much wider expansion.The muskrat's European advance therefore became useful to scientists studying biological invasions. Because its spread occurred over decades and was recorded in different countries, it offered an unusually detailed example of how a non-native mammal can establish itself, expand and reach a new geographical limit.Why European countries keep trapping muskratsThe problem with muskrats in Europe has little to do with their appearance. Their burrowing habits can cause serious trouble where waterways have been engineered by people. A natural riverbank can tolerate a certain amount of excavation. A flood embankment, canal bank or railway embankment has a different purpose.Muskrats excavate entrances below the waterline and can create networks of tunnels inside earthen banks. Repeated burrowing may weaken those structures, particularly where large numbers of animals are present.That turned the species into more than a nuisance for landowners. In countries that depend heavily on engineered water defences, controlling muskrat populations became part of maintaining infrastructure. Much of the country relies on dikes, embankments and other barriers to manage water, so animals capable of burrowing into those structures are treated as a practical threat. Muskrat trapping became a permanent operation, with professional trappers working throughout the year and removing large numbers of animals.The objective is not simply to reduce the population in one field or canal. Dutch authorities have pursued the much harder task of keeping the species from spreading further into the country.Belgium, France and Germany have also maintained control programmes. According to the National Parks & Wildlife Service, in 2017, the European Union formally placed the muskrat on its list of invasive alien species of Union concern. The designation brings restrictions intended to prevent the animal from being kept, transported, traded or deliberately released.How Britain managed to eradicate muskrats by 1939There is one particularly unusual chapter in the European story. Muskrats reached Britain through the fur trade rather than from the original Dobříš population. Escapes from fur farms during the late 1920s allowed them to establish themselves, particularly around waterways in the Severn region.According to the study published in Biological Journal of the Linnean Society, titled, ‘The eradication of muskrats and coypus from Britain Get access Arrow’, reveals that Britain responded with a large-scale eradication programme. The campaign lasted years and required sustained trapping rather than a single intervention. By 1939, the established British muskrat population had been eliminated. Once an invasive mammal becomes widespread across interconnected habitats, removing every remaining animal becomes vastly more difficult than preventing the initial establishment.Britain's experience showed that eradication could work under the right circumstances, particularly when the population was still geographically limited and resources could be concentrated on the affected area.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Did Twitch suspend LowTierGod for 14 days? ‘Derogatory’ remarks blamed as streamer moves to Kick
articles.summary: US Streamers News: Controversial streamer Dalauan “LowTierGod” Prince, also known as LTG, has claimed that Twitch suspended his account for 14 days over derogatory remar.
articles.body: Controversial streamer Dalauan “LowTierGod” Prince, also known as LTG, has claimed that Twitch suspended his account for 14 days over derogatory remarks made during a recent livestream. Speaking on Kick on August 31, 2026, LTG said he would stream exclusively on the platform for the next two weeks because of the alleged Twitch suspension. However, his Twitch channel was still accessible at the time of writing, so the suspension had not been independently confirmed. LTG also showed viewers the footage that he believed led to the alleged action.LowTierGod claims his Twitch suspension followed offensive remarksDuring his August 31 Kick livestream, LTG said he expected to spend the next two weeks streaming only on Kick.He then looked back at a recent VOD while discussing what he believed had caused the alleged Twitch suspension. LTG said the issue involved remarks about Africans and people he referred to as “Rashids.”He said:“All right, so, looks like we are going to be on Kick for like two ****** weeks exclusively because I, you know, when it comes to me, just everything that I do is so bad.”LTG then played part of the earlier livestream. In the clip, he made several derogatory comments about Africans and other groups, including references to their food, living conditions and religion.Because the remarks contain repeated offensive language and ethnic and religious insults, the comments are not reproduced in full here.LTG said Twitch’s alleged action was connected to those comments and argued that he was being treated too harshly.There is an important distinction between LTG’s claim and what has been independently established. His Twitch channel had not been taken down when the report was prepared, and there was no publicly confirmed Twitch statement about a 14-day suspension. As a result, the exact status of his Twitch account remained unclear.LowTierGod says a two-week ban could hurt his streaming momentumLTG also explained why he believed a 14-day suspension would have a bigger impact than simply missing two weeks of broadcasts.The streamer said losing access to Twitch for the first half of September could affect his numbers and momentum for the following month. He argued that returning after a forced break would leave him with less time to maintain the same level of activity on the platform.LTG said:“This is why ****** quit streaming over there, dude. You get banned for any ******* thing!”He went on to explain his concerns about the timing of the alleged suspension.“If I'm banned for 14 days, it kills my entire momentum, and it ***** over my whole, like, it ***** over my whole month next month.”LTG said that two weeks away from Twitch would mean having to make up for the lost activity later.“That means the first two weeks of September will literally be like I did nothing on the platform.”He also questioned why he believed Twitch was paying such close attention to his content.“I don't know why the **** am I under the microscope for miniscule ****.”LTG has faced controversy several times throughout his streaming career, and his comments about the alleged Twitch suspension have now added another dispute involving the platform.For now, the key detail remains unconfirmed: LTG says Twitch suspended him for 14 days, but his channel was still available and no public Twitch confirmation of the alleged suspension was available at the time of writing.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Drunk man steals plane, sends fighter jets scrambling near nuclear plant
articles.summary: While intoxicated, a 24-year-old man allegedly stole a Cessna 172 from an airport in Hungary. He flew toward a nuclear power plant and triggered fighter jets to respond.
articles.body: A 24-year-old man allegedly stole a small plane from an airport in Hungary while intoxicated before prompting a dramatic military response — a "very dangerous" and "rare" occurrence, according to an aviation expert. The man took a Cessna 172 from Kalocsa Airport on Saturday morning after pulling the ropes that secured the plane from the ground, according to a translated video posted on Facebook by Hungarian police. The man then took off using a service road and headed toward Paks, home to Hungary's only nuclear power plant, according to a Facebook post from Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi, Ph.D., Hungary's defense minister. TSA OFFICER SEES ALARMING SHAPES ON X-RAY BEFORE STOLEN CIVIL WAR MYSTERY UNRAVELS Hungarian military radars detected the aircraft, prompting a pair of standby fighter jets to take off, Ruszin-Szendi said. The Cessna later came down in a sunflower field near Gerjen — where the fighter jets located the damaged aircraft and remained overhead until rescue crews arrived, the post said. The pilot suffered minor injuries during the landing and made his way through the field to a nearby road, according to the translated video. A passing driver stopped after the man asked for help — but the 24-year-old then allegedly attempted to take the vehicle, according to a translated press release from Hungarian police. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER The driver prevented him from leaving with the car — and responding officers, within minutes, apprehended the suspect nearby, police said. Authorities said the man appeared to be intoxicated at the time of the incident. "According to our current information, the man was drunk, and the police are investigating whether he was under the influence of other drugs," Hungarian police said in the translated release. Fox News Digital reached out to the Hungarian police for further comment and details. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES Authorities are investigating the circumstances surrounding the plane theft with aviation officials and other experts. The suspect was taken into custody and faces charges related to the incident, police said. "The effects of alcohol can be extreme." "For someone operating an aircraft without any experience whatsoever, or limited experience, it could be very dangerous," said Steven Arroyo, an aviation expert and retired airline captain based in Florida (he is not involved in the investigation of the case in Hungary). "Stealing [an] aircraft and going out on joyrides is extremely rare," he added. "It's really not a major event that occurs on a regular basis — but it's a serious event [when it] occurs. There are strict regulations in terms of consuming alcohol if you are behind the controls of an aircraft. Those rules are worldwide." TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ There can be a "severe impairment of judgment, especially when you gain altitude because the air is thinner, so the bloodstream is getting reduced oxygen. … The effects of alcohol can be extreme," he added. Fox News Digital previously reported on another Cessna theft involving a small plane at Van Nuys Airport in Los Angeles in December 2025. A 37-year-old man allegedly gained access to the airport and a Cessna C172 before the aircraft struck a hangar, according to Los Angeles Airport Police and the Federal Aviation Administration. The plane was never airborne and hit the building while taxiing, according to reports. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The suspect was taken into custody on suspicion of burglary and aircraft theft. Bonny Chu of Fox News Digital contributed reporting.

articles.title: Hollywood actor Joel McCrea bought a California ranch in 1933; his family later donated 74 acres as a wildlife preserve and effectively gave another 220 acres for parkland
articles.summary: US News: When Hollywood western actor Joel McCrea bought a large piece of farmland in Santa Rosa Valley in 1933, he wanted a quiet working retreat away from mo.
articles.body: When Hollywood western actor Joel McCrea bought a large piece of farmland in Santa Rosa Valley in 1933, he wanted a quiet working retreat away from movie sets. Decades later, the property has moved into public ownership, helping protect hundreds of acres of open land and natural habitat along the northern edge of Thousand Oaks, California. Through land transfers and open space donations made by his family, the former 3,000-acre working ranch has provided important areas for conservation. The family officially donated 74 acres as a protected wildlife sanctuary, while also helping arrange the public purchase of another 220 acres to remain as parkland and historic open space. According to records from the Conejo Open Space Conservation Agency, the 74-acre preserve includes rocky cliffs, deep canyons and groups of rare native plants. High sandstone bluffs provide important nesting and resting areas for birds of prey, while a year-round water source helps support wildlife in the area. To protect the sensitive environment, access to the 74-acre wildlife area is strictly limited. The sanctuary contains protected stands of the rare Conejo rock plant, a plant found almost entirely in this particular part of Ventura County.Transition from private ranch to public parklandThe larger 220-acre section containing the historic ranch buildings was transferred to public management through an agreement between the McCrea family and local park officials. Reports archived by the Los Angeles Times say the agreement allowed the Conejo Recreation and Park District to acquire the home and surrounding property, protecting it from future suburban development. The deal was helped by a friendship between the actor and Tex Ward, who served as general manager emeritus of the park district. Their relationship helped the family transfer the main ranch property to the district, allowing the surrounding open hillsides to remain protected. McCrea originally bought the land on the advice of his close friend and mentor Will Rogers. Rogers famously encouraged young Hollywood actors to invest in farmland as protection against the uncertain nature of the film business. McCrea and his wife, actress Frances Dee, built their main home there in 1933. They raised their three sons while running a working cattle and grain farm. The property was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1997. Records filed with the National Park Service say the site has eight historic buildings, including a main house designed by architect John Byers. The house was different from Byers’ better-known Spanish Colonial Revival designs and instead showed an early form of the simple California ranch style.Legacy of conservation in the Conejo ValleyDuring the mid-20th century, urban growth changed much of Ventura County. The McCrea family gradually sold parts of their larger landholdings, helping create some of the early land base of Thousand Oaks. The family later donated other parcels to non-profit organisations, including land used to establish the local YMCA branch. After McCrea died in 1990, his family worked to protect the final 280 acres of the original property. The Conejo Recreation and Park District later built a visitor centre on the site. It now works with the Joel and Frances McCrea Ranch Foundation to offer educational programmes, historic tours and environmental activities. Public agencies have also continued to expand the protected area around the historic ranch. Park officials later bought a nearby 33-acre hillside grassland parcel. A separate residential development agreement also transferred another 55-acre open space area of steep ridgeline land to conservation authorities. The historic ranch complex, located at the foot of the historic Norwegian Grade road, remains open through scheduled educational programmes organised by local park officials. Restoration work funded by the ranch foundation continues to protect the surviving buildings, preserving both the valley’s farming history and its surrounding natural landscape.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Hakainde Hichilema returns as Zambia’s president following disputed vote
articles.summary: Incumbent is inaugurated with his main rival in last month’s election jailed and the courts shuttered.
articles.body:
President Hakainde Hichilema has been sworn in for a second term as Zambia’s president following his victory in disputed elections.

As Hichilema was inaugurated at the National Heroes Stadium in the Zambian capital Lusaka on Tuesday, his main rival in last month’s election was in detention , accused of treason as allegations of vote rigging persisted.

Leaders and dignitaries from several countries, including the United States and China, flew in for the ceremony, during which the president pledged to rule with equality.

“We receive your support with humility and with a clear understanding of the responsibility it places upon our shoulders. To those who chose other candidates or other parties, we say with equal sincerity: We have heard you,” Hichilema said.

The day after the August 13 election that secured a second term for Hichilema, police raided the home of runner-up Brian Mundubile, during which a former cabinet member was shot and killed.

Mundubile and his running mate Makebi Zulu were arrested on Thursday charged with treason, after spending two weeks seeking refuge with an international human rights organisation.

Police have not provided details of the allegations underpinning the charges. Both deny any wrongdoing.

Around a dozen other opposition figures who have questioned the election result have been arrested. The authorities abruptly closed the country’s courts last week.

US-based Human Rights Watch has criticised the move, saying it prevents the opposition from filing legal challenges against the vote.

Hichilema was re-elected after securing 60 percent of the vote. Mundubile secured 38 percent of ballots cast, but alleges that the election was rigged.

Addressing thousands of jubilant supporters as he was sworn in, Hichilema pledged to continue improving Zambia’s economy. He oversaw the restructuring of the country’s debt during his first term, while also attracting international investment and reducing inflation.

Hichilema’s running mate, Mutale Nalumango, was sworn in as vice-president at the same ceremony.

Tanzania’s President Samia Suluhu Hassan was among the attendees and congratulated Hichilema on his re-election in a post on X. The presidents of Botswana, Kenya and Zimbabwe were also present.

images.caption: Zambia's President Hakainde Hichilema inspects the guard of honour on the day of his swearing-in ceremony in Lusaka, Zambia, September 1 [Jean Mandela/Reuters]

articles.title: Andy Burnham promises more devolution and public control of essential services
articles.summary: Tory leader Kemi Badenoch said Burnham was offering "more government control, more taxes and more politicians", as he addressed MPs for the first time as PM.
articles.body:
Andy Burnham has promised to set out plans for "stronger public control" of essential services as he addressed the House of Commons for the first time since taking power.

The prime minister said "a series of wrong turns" since the 1980s had seen economic power in the UK privatised and pointed to the water industry as "a leaking monument to that approach - a country run in the private rather than public interest".

He reiterated his belief that political power had been centralised and announced he would be making devolution powers available to more areas in England.

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch accused Burnham of offering "more government control, more taxes and more politicians".

"His diagnosis is completely wrong, his theory of growth is completely wrong, he thinks that if government spends more money, we will all get richer - that is not how this works," she said.

Badenoch also warned the prime minister that his new job would be "very different" to his previous Greater Manchester mayoral role where he "did not have to make difficult trade-offs".

Burnham became prime minister on 20 July shortly after Parliament closed for the summer recess.

Tuesday marked the first day of the new parliamentary session and provided his first opportunity to address MPs and take questions.

He told the House of Commons that "Britain is not where we would wish it to be", but promised to "build a new sense of optimism around the country".

Following his 10 years away from Parliament, Burnham said he was returning with a "clear diagnosis" of what had gone wrong in the country.

"From the 1980s, this country took a series of wrong turns," he said.

"Political power was centralised, economic power privatised, the country deindustrialised, austerity followed, hollowing out councils and depriving them of the agency to act to reverse any of this.

"And then Brexit compounded the damage, ushering in a decade of low growth and stalled regeneration."

In the months before becoming prime minister, Burnham stopped short of calling for full nationalisation but said he wanted to see greater public control of water and energy.

On Tuesday, he promised that a plan to achieve this would be produced "later in the year".

Pressed on his plans for the water sector by Conservative MP Alison Griffiths, Burnham said it was important to "look at all possible solutions".

"It's a very regrettable situation that the privatisation of water has left us in a position where we're going to find it very difficult to reverse," he added.

Burnham's summer tour is over - now he has to prove himself in Parliament

Andy Burnham's first week pledges - how much do they add up to?

Five takeaways from Burnham's Commons debut as PM

Burnham said his time as Greater Manchester mayor had given him "a clear theory of growth", namely that devolving powers to regions outside London would boost their economy.

He argued the approach had worked in Manchester and now he wanted "every single place across our regions and nations to be able to do the same, creating the conditions for good growth in every postcode".

Some MPs have raised concern that areas without mayors - and the new powers that have come with them - would suffer, leading to a two-tier system.

Efforts to secure a devolution deal in Cornwall have been stymied by the county's reluctance to form a group with Devon but also to having a mayor.

Burnham appeared to have accepted the county's concerns, telling the House of Commons his government would work with Cornwall Council and its six MPs on a devolution deal "with or without an elected mayor".

He added that he would be extending "the same offer to all parts of England without devolved power".

He also said he was interested in exploring "a local model of devolution" in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.

Shortly before Burnham's speech to Parliament, Sir Keir Starmer said in a surprise announcement that he would be stepping down as an MP, less than two months after he quit as prime minister.

Burnham began his speech by paying tribute to his predecessor telling the House of Commons that Sir Keir had "given this country a lifetime of public service" and created a "platform to change this country for the better".

In his wide-ranging statement, which lasted three-and-half-hours, Burnham gave an indication of his approach on several other issues including welfare.

He suggested that providing more council homes and thereby bringing down rent for more people would be the "Labour way" of reducing the benefits bill.

The prime minister also committed to introducing legislation that would allow homeowners to move more easily from the leasehold system to a commonhold form of ownership.

Asked by Badenoch about defence spending, Burnham said he had specifically chosen John Healey to be his chancellor because of his "commitment to defence".

Healey resigned as defence secretary earlier this year, accusing then-prime minister Sir Keir of failing to commit the resources needed to keep the country safe.

Liberal Democrat leader Sir Ed Davey used his question to argue that too much power in the UK was in "the wrong hands" and called for "fundamental change" of the political system.

Burnham said he would look at the voting system but would not introduce any changes before the next general election.

articles.title: Jasontheween x Valkyrae: Maybach Monday date, time and Twitch details
articles.summary: US Streamers News: Jasontheween has announced Valkyrae as the next guest for his popular Maybach Monday series. The streamer shared a poster for the upcoming episode on .
articles.body: Jasontheween has announced Valkyrae as the next guest for his popular Maybach Monday series. The streamer shared a poster for the upcoming episode on X, revealing that the livestream will take place on September 2, 2026. Fans can watch it on Jasontheween’s Twitch channel at 12 PM PST, 3 PM EST, 8 PM GMT and 9 PM CET. For viewers in India, the stream will begin at 1:30 AM IST on September 3. The announcement has already attracted plenty of reactions, with fans suggesting activities they want the two creators to try during the show.Jasontheween and Valkyrae set for Maybach Monday streamMaybach Monday has become a regular part of Jasontheween’s content, with the streamer bringing different guests onto his broadcast for conversations, activities and interactions with viewers.This time, Valkyrae will join him for the next episode.The announcement came through an official post on X, where Jasontheween shared the promotional poster and details for the stream. The episode is scheduled for September 2 at 12 PM PST, which is 3 PM EST, 8 PM GMT and 9 PM CET. Indian viewers can catch it at 1:30 AM IST on September 3.The livestream will be available on Jasontheween’s Twitch channel.Fans were quick to react to the announcement. Some were simply excited to see Valkyrae appear on the show, while others already had ideas for possible segments.One viewer suggested bringing Pokémon cards into the stream because of Valkyrae’s interest in trading card games.“Do a segment with rae ripping pokemon cards she's hella into tcg.”Another fan wrote:“WE’LL BE THERE TRUST.”A third viewer added:“I can't wait for tomorrow.”With Valkyrae joining the show, viewers will now have to wait for the stream to see what Jasontheween has planned for the episode.Jasontheween wants to bring his parents to the CORE houseValkyrae is not the only thing Jasontheween has been discussing recently. During another stream, a viewer asked him about his plans for future vlogs.Jason then revealed that he wanted to bring his parents to the CORE house for about a week. He also had a specific idea for the content: filming his father driving his new car.He said:“You know what I want to vlog? I want to get my parents out here. I want to vlog my dad driving my new car. I think I’m gonna fly my parents out here for like a week. I think that would be generational. That’d be so funny.”The streamer was then asked whether he planned to livestream the visit or turn it into a vlog.Jason initially considered doing it live but quickly changed his mind.“Maybe, maybe streaming. Nah, nah. I’ll probably do a little video.”His comments suggest that the family visit would most likely become a separate video rather than a full livestream. He did not give a date for when he plans to bring his parents to the CORE house.For now, the confirmed upcoming event is his Maybach Monday episode with Valkyrae on September 2. Fans will be able to see what the pair have planned when the stream goes live on Jasontheween’s Twitch channel.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: One glaring issue goes unaddressed in UN chief's high-stakes talks with Iran's president
articles.summary: António Guterres met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, but a U.N. readout omitted any mention of detained protesters or torture allegations.
articles.body: United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian Tuesday as Iranians detained from January's nationwide protests continue to face prison sentences, alleged torture and a growing number of death sentences and executions. The U.N. readout of the meeting, held on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit in Bishkek, said Guterres raised the humanitarian and economic consequences of the conflict involving Iran and stressed the need for diplomacy and respect for international law. The readout made no mention of Iran's treatment of protesters, executions or allegations of torture. Asked by Fox News Digital at Tuesday's U.N. briefing whether Guterres raised those issues directly with Pezeshkian, and if so, why they were not included in the readout, the secretary-general's spokesperson, Stéphane Dujarric, said he had "nothing to add to the readout." 'KILLING OFF THE COUNTRY': IRAN EXECUTES DOZENS, ARRESTS 4,000-PLUS IN WAR CRACKDOWN But Dujarric said Guterres had raised the issues with senior Iranian officials in other meetings. "I can tell you that in other meetings with senior Iranian leaders, in New York and other places, the secretary-general has raised those issues directly," Dujarric said. "We have, from this podium, on behalf of the secretary-general, condemned in no uncertain terms the use of the death penalty in Iran, as we stand against the death penalty in every country." The exchange comes as human rights organizations report that Tehran's crackdown has continued months after the January demonstrations. Iran International reported Aug. 7, citing rights groups, that more than 60,000 people were detained across Iran after the protests, while some independent sources put the number of people summoned, detained or interrogated above 100,000. IRAN HANGS 2 PROTESTERS IN PUBLIC; CROWD CRIES 'DISHONORABLE' AS SECURITY FIRES TEAR GAS In Ardabil province alone, roughly 800 people were arrested during the protests, according to the report, which cited the Human Rights Activists News Agency, or HRANA. As of early August, at least 54 remained in Ardabil Prison, including 29 who had not yet received a hearing. New figures released Tuesday show the punishments have continued. In its monthly report published Sept. 1, HRANA said it documented 78 executions across Iran in August, including two people executed in connection with the January protests. Iranian courts issued 21 death sentences during the month, including against 10 defendants in an Isfahan case stemming from the protests. The group also documented six cases of forced confessions, four cases of prisoners being beaten, four transfers to solitary confinement and nine cases in which detainees were denied access to legal counsel. HRANA reported Aug. 31 that 13 people arrested during January protests were sentenced to a combined 24 years, three months and one day in prison. Four of the defendants also received a combined 196 lashes, while one was sentenced to two years of exile. The crackdown has also increasingly involved capital punishment. Iran International reported Aug. 26, citing HRANA, that two additional January protest detainees had been sentenced to death. The same report cited the U.S.-based Abdorrahman Boroumand Center as saying it had documented 950 executions in Iran since the beginning of 2026, including at least 30 protesters. INSIDE TEHRAN: IRANIANS DESCRIBE IRGC'S BRUTAL RULE, POVERTY — ASK TRUMP TO 'STAY THE COURSE' Among those imprisoned is Seyed Ahmad Seyedabdollahi, a 32-year-old psychologist whose case Fox News Digital reported in August. Seyedabdollahi posted an English-language video Jan. 4 appealing directly to President Donald Trump to support Iranian protesters. He was arrested 10 days later and ultimately sentenced to seven months in prison and barred from government and public services for five years. His relatives told Fox News Digital that Iranian authorities later pressured him to record another video insulting Trump and Americans. Fox News Digital could not independently verify those specific demands, but IranWire reported Aug. 11 that security agents instructed him to read a prepared anti-Trump script on camera and that he repeatedly refused despite alleged threats and coercion. His relatives also alleged that Seyedabdollahi was subjected to solitary confinement and torture. Hana Human Rights Organization reported Aug. 9 that he had been held in Borujen Prison since July 7 and that authorities opened a second case against him on a charge of "propaganda against the system of the Islamic Republic." WALTZ CALLS OUT IRANIAN DIPLOMAT AT UN FOLLOWING DRONE STRIKES ON BAHRAIN AND KUWAIT The fate of Iran's detainees also surfaced Tuesday at the U.N. Security Council as France assumed the rotating presidency for September. The Security Council's official presidency list shows France holding the September presidency, with Ambassador Jérôme Bonnafont serving as council president. Asked by Fox News Digital whether France planned to address Iranians detained after the protests and reports of torture and executions during its presidency, Bonnafont said the council's central focus on Iran this month would be Tehran's nuclear program but stressed that those discussions would not take place "in a vacuum." "You referred to this matter with the situation of the civilian population in Iran," Bonnafont told Fox News Digital, according to a translation of his remarks. "They are the victims of the choices made by the Iranian authorities for years now, with these episodes of mass repression to which you referred." Morad Tahbaz, an Iranian American environmentalist who spent years imprisoned in Iran before his release in a 2023 prisoner exchange with the United States, previously described to Fox News Digital the conditions detainees can face inside the Iranian prison system. Tahbaz said he spent four months alone in a small cell under a bright light that remained on 24 hours a day. He was allowed out twice a day for about 10 minutes and was blindfolded whenever he left the cell. He described the IRGC intelligence facility at Tehran's Evin Prison as "probably the harshest and toughest imprisonment that any prisoner will go through." Tahbaz said one of the most difficult aspects of being held by Iran was knowing that even the end of a prison sentence did not necessarily mean freedom. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "When you are a hostage … [you don't know that], at the end of your sentence, they'll necessarily let you go," Tahbaz told Fox News Digital. "They'll just come up with another charge to keep you there for as long as you're of value to them."

articles.title: Swimmer rushed to hospital after suspected shark attack at Martha’s Vineyard
articles.summary: Swimming was temporarily suspended at South Beach in Edgartown after a woman sustained injuries considered consistent with a potential shark bite.
articles.body: Emergency personnel from Martha’s Vineyard rushed a swimmer to a hospital Monday after the woman sustained what appeared to be a shark bite, officials said. The incident happened in the afternoon at South Beach in Edgartown, Massachusetts, along one of the island’s most popular shorelines. Officials said the victim, in her late 20s, was in the water when she suffered a wound to her lower leg. SHARK WEEK PUTS SHARK BITE SURVIVAL IN FOCUS WITH ER DOC'S EXPERT TIPS "Based upon the nature of the injuries, however, the wounds were considered consistent with a potential shark bite," Town Administrator James Hagerty said in a statement. Her injuries were considered non-life-threatening and "did not involve the loss of a limb or other life-threatening trauma," Hagerty said. Multiple Edgartown agencies responded, and the woman received initial medical treatment before being transported to a hospital for further care. After the suspected shark encounter, no marine predators were observed or confirmed that were involved the incident, officials said. SHARK SIGHTINGS SPIKE NEAR AMERICA'S BEACHES AS JULY 4 CROWDS HEAD TO SHORE FOR WEEKEND In accordance with town protocol, officials suspended swimming at South Beach for several hours as a precaution, allowing personnel to assess conditions before later lifting the water restrictions. The town thanked emergency personnel and beach staff for their prompt response. SHARK WEEK WARNINGS AS EXPERTS REVEAL 6 WAYS TO REDUCE YOUR RISK OF A SHARK BITE "Beachgoers are reminded to remain aware of their surroundings while in the water and to comply with instructions from lifeguards and any posted beach advisories," Hagerty said. Confirmed shark attacks near Martha’s Vineyard have historically been rare, though marine predators are known to pass through the area. Nearly all serious or fatal shark attacks in Massachusetts over the last two decades have occurred along the coast of nearby Cape Cod, which is two hours away by car. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Cape Cod is considered a major hot spot for great white sharks in the North Atlantic due to its large population of gray seals, a primary food source for the predators.

articles.title: 7 Best Vegan and Vegetarian Meal Delivery Services of 2026
articles.summary: Find some of the best meal delivery services with vegetarian and vegan options. Get vegetarian meal kits from Sunbasket, Blue Apron, Splendid Spoon and more.
articles.body: Whether you’re eating at a restaurant or shopping for groceries, there’s typically no shortage of vegetarian and vegan options to choose from. Meal delivery services are no exception: Many popular meal kits and ready-made meals offer flexible plans to fit most dietary restrictions, including vegetarian, gluten-free and dairy-free diets. Meal delivery services that include vegetarian and vegan plans can provide easy-to-cook or ready-made meat-free meals and prevent you from having to sprint to the supermarket each week. If you’re ready to sign up for a meal delivery plan but don’t know where to start, I spoke to nutritionists and recipe developers about services they think are worth considering and compiled their favorite ones that include vegetarian and vegan plans. I also rounded up meal delivery services I and other NBC Selected staffers have tried and love. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. Best vegan and vegetarian meal delivery services “Nowadays, there are meal delivery services specifically catered towards more challenging dietary restrictions —[they] can make it easier to find meals you can safely tolerate when you can’t always rely on unfamiliar restaurants,” says Lisa Moskovitz, a registered dietitian and CEO of NY Nutrition Group. Each of the following meal delivery services comes recommended by our food experts and/or NBC Selected editors who have tested them. All of them offer either completely plant-based vegetarian or vegan services, or they offer specific plans to fit one of these lifestyles. To make your browsing easier, I note the starting price, serving size and number of meals provided by each service. Best overall Sunbasket has both meal kits and pre-made, non-frozen meals (although you can freeze some of them to cook later, in line with the brand’s cooking instructions). NBC Selected reporter Zoe Malin tried Sunbasket for a week and loved how varied the options were for her gluten-free and pescatarian diet. “I can usually only eat one or two offerings off a meal delivery service’s weekly menu. But with Sunbasket, there were almost too many delicious dishes to choose from,” she says. Malin also loves the service’s pre-made meals, which taste like homemade meals without needing to put in the work, she says. Sunbasket has a variety of options that you can, depending on whether you eat meat or strictly follow a plant-based diet, says Moskovitz. One of the service’s nine meal plans is the vegetarian plan, which comes with a variety of meal kits to choose from that are focused on protein, good fats and fiber, according to the brand. If you don’t feel like committing to just one type of plan, Sunbasket lets you mix and match its Fresh & Ready plan with over a dozen meal kits from its weekly rotating menu. Best for beginners Blue Apron has a number of weekly menu items based on your selected meal plan. Its vegetarian plan offers nutritionist-approved recipes made with fruits, vegetables, grains, seeds and more, which can be created with or without dairy products, honey and eggs, according to the brand. The plan serves two people and includes two to five meat-free recipes per week (depending on your plan preferences), most of which you can prepare in 25 to 35 minutes, according to Blue Apron. Best budget-friendly “HelloFresh offers quick and easy chef-curated recipes, they use fresh, sustainably sourced ingredients and [they] offer vegan and vegetarian options,” says Lisa Young, adjunct professor of nutrition at New York University. I tested HelloFresh and it quickly became one of my favorite services — I love that the recipes are easy to follow (which, as a non-cook, is key for me) and the meal options are both tasty and varied. The meal kit service has over 30 recipes to choose from each week, and you can customize your plan with protein-specific preferences: beef-free, pork-free, seafood-free and veggie. Though choosing the veggie preference doesn’t change the weekly rotating menu HelloFresh provides, it does ensure that you automatically receive meat-free meals for that given menu week. The brand offers 10 veggie meals (including one vegan meal) within its Classic Plan each week — vegetarian recipes can also be made vegan by opting to remove certain ingredients like cheese or yogurt, according to the brand. The veggie and vegan meals are labeled under each recipe, so you can see which recipes fit your dietary needs when crafting your menu each week. Best health-conscious Splendid Spoon has a menu of more than 50 healthy, ready-made vegan meals and snacks to choose from, including smoothies, soups and entrees, all of which have no meat, dairy or animal byproduct. You can order subscription boxes of five meals or more. The service also offers a five-day detox program, in which you get five days worth of meals. “I recommend Splendid Spoon for anyone who wants healthy meals in a flash — they taste as healthy as they are, which is a downside for some and a bonus for others,” says Ariane Resnick, a special diet chef and certified nutritionist. The brand sent me a few options of their smoothies, entrees, detox shots and soups to try out, and I loved the variety of flavors. The soups and entrees are also easy to prepare, and I can freeze them to eat later (which is great if I’m traveling that week). The smoothies, which come in more than a dozen delicious flavors, kept me full throughout the day, so I didn’t find myself binging on unhealthy snacks in the afternoon. The soups were my favorite part of the service: Not only did they taste great, but they also come in fairly large portions, so they were filling and served as a healthy alternative for lunch or dinner. Splendid Spoon lets you choose how often you want to receive your meals: weekly, biweekly, every three weeks or monthly. Best all plant-based meals Purple Carrot has both prepared meals and meal kits, both of which are fully plant-based and vegan. The meals are a perfect mix of familiar and innovative, says Resnick, who adds that, “it’s an easy way for people to add more plant foods into their diets without having to fully convert to veganism.” You can customize the number of prepared dinners you get per week — which range from six to 10 frozen meals — or choose three or four recipes from its weekly rotating menu for meal kits each week. Deliveries take place on Mondays, Tuesdays or Wednesdays depending on your shipping location, and you can choose to skip a delivery on any given week. Best ready-made vegetarian meals Get $130 off, plus free wellness shots for life with code NBCSELECT130 through Factor’s website. Factor has a weekly rotating menu of over 27 pre-prepared meals designed by dieticians — you can choose the service’s Veggie + Vegan plan for plant-based recipes that are free of all animal products, including meat, fish, eggs and dairy, according to the service. I tried Factor for a week and found it quick, convenient and tasty, which is great for busy weekdays when I don’t have time to cook. Young also recommends this service specifically because it caters to a number of diets and dietary needs, including keto, paleo, low-carb, vegetarian and high-protein. You can choose from five plans, ranging from four meals per week up to 18 meals per week. Best splurge All of Sakara’s ready-made meals are vegan, plant-based and gluten-free, as well as organic and dairy-free, according to the service. “Sakara is very popular among my clients because of [its] varied menu, top-quality ingredients and delicious taste,” says Moskovitz. Programs include the Signature Nutrition Program, which comes with up to three meals per day and your choice of two, three or five days, and the Metabolism Reset, a one-, four- or eight-week program that sends you a specifically curated menu for up to five days per week. You can choose to do a one-week trial program if you’re just getting started, or you can pick a recurring subscription program that automatically renews each week with a set menu of meals that rotates weekly and seasonally. How to shop for vegan and vegetarian meal delivery services When shopping for a vegan- or vegetarian-friendly meal delivery service, our experts recommend keeping in mind the following factors: Plant-based plans: Look for services that offer plant-based or fully vegan meal plans. Many services will offer several vegan and vegetarian options within their weekly menu, and you can update your preferences to automatically show these meals.Serving size: If you’re feeding multiple family members who follow a vegetarian or vegan diet, you’ll want to consider meal kits with multiple serving sizes (typically ranging from two to eight servings). If you’re just feeding yourself, it’s probably best to select a single-serve prepared meal. Customizability: Browse services that provide a weekly rotating menu with several vegan and vegetarian options that you can select or swap in.Delivery dates and times: Many services will offer customizable plans to choose which days (and sometimes times) you want to receive your kit. Most will also let you pause plans or skip weeks as needed. Meet our culinary experts At NBC Selected, we work with experts who have specialized knowledge and authority based on relevant training and/or experience. We also take steps to ensure that all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and with no undisclosed financial conflicts of interest. Lisa Moskovitz is a registered dietitian and the CEO of NY Nutrition Group. She is the author of “The Core 3 Healthy Eating Plan,” a program that focuses on simple and sustainable ways to lose weight.Ben Leonard is a chef and educator for companies and brands nationwide, including Sur La Table, Greenpan and more.Lisa Young is an adjunct professor of nutrition in the Department of Nutrition and Food Studies at New York University.Ariane Resnick is a special diet chef and certified nutritionist. She’s also a recipe developer and has written about nutrition, health, wellness and identity for a variety of platforms, including The Kitchn, Livestrong and Simply Recipes.Abby K. Cannon is a dietician and the founder of Abby’s Food Court, a private nutrition practice that focuses on women’s health and eco-friendly lifestyles. Why trust NBC Selected? I’m an updates editor at NBC Selected who has written about meal delivery services for over three years. For this article, I spoke to chefs and nutritionists about what to look for in a vegetarian and vegan meal delivery service, and gathered their recommendations for the best ones to try out. Catch up on NBC Selected’s in-depth coverage of tech and tools, wellness and more, and follow us on Facebook, Instagram, Twitter and TikTok to stay up to date.

articles.title: College student steps into traffic, is killed after losing immigration status
articles.summary: A Haitian immigrant who had grown increasingly distraught after losing his protection from deportation and being outfitted with an ankle monitor was run over...
articles.body:
A Haitian immigrant who had grown increasingly distraught after losing his protection from deportation and being outfitted with an ankle monitor was run over and killed Monday in what his family believes was a suicide.

Pierre Damas Bel, 20, parked on the shoulder of Interstate 70 in Springfield, Ohio, sometime before 8:45 a.m., got out of his vehicle and walked into westbound traffic, the Ohio State Highway Patrol said. He was hit by a tractor-trailer and pronounced dead at the scene.

Like an estimated 350,000 Haitian immigrants, Bel had recently lost temporary protected status, which is given to people fleeing nations experiencing disaster, his family said. He had a pending asylum claim but had been summoned to an Immigration and Customs Enforcement office after the Supreme Court allowed the Trump administration to proceed with canceling the status for Haitian recipients. Federal immigration agents placed an electronic monitoring device on his ankle, which is one way the agency tracks immigrants it is seeking to remove from the country.

"He felt like he was treated like an animal," his father, Pierres Ronal Bel, 40, recounted in a handwritten statement.

Ohio authorities said they are investigating the crash.

The Department of Homeland Security declined to comment on the circumstances of Bel's death while the investigation is ongoing. The Trump administration has been calling Haitian immigrants into ICE offices to be equipped with ankle monitors and has sent two deportation flights to Haiti since temporary protected status was canceled for people from the troubled Caribbean nation. Advocates for the immigrants say the U.S. government is sending people back to a country where criminal gangs are responsible for massacres, kidnapping and extortion.

Haitian leaders in Springfield and beyond said Bel's death is symptomatic of the extreme stress many immigrants are under as they fear being detained and sent back.

"These policies are what caused his untimely death," said Guerline Jozef of the Haitian Bridge Alliance, a nonprofit that provides legal and humanitarian aid to migrants.

Bel came to the U.S. in 2024 to reunite with his parents, who had fled Haiti three years before. ICE said its records show he entered through CBP One, the mobile app the Biden administration established for immigrants to enter the country at a port of entry and request asylum.

The family was granted temporary protected status, purchased a home in Springfield and settled into life in the U.S. Bel dreamed of studying medicine and graduated from high school in May with honors and as a proud member of the Junior Reserve Officer Training Corps (JROTC), his father said. He was the eldest of three siblings, and his family described him as smart and responsible.

The young man's Instagram account is full of photos of himself smiling in his JROTC uniform and displaying his diploma and various academic awards.

Bel wanted to continue life as a cadet in the program but was distressed by what transpired after temporary protected status was canceled for Haitians. His father said he couldn't play soccer as he had for years because of the weight of the tracker. Classmates bullied him and made cruel remarks. He begged federal immigration officers to remove the bracelet, his father said, but they refused.

"I came to this country to pursue my education. I didn't come here to commit a crime or hurt anyone," he wrote on Instagram in late July. "Yet now I'm walking through the streets of the United States with a GPS monitor on my leg, carrying a feeling of shame and humiliation that I never imagined I would experience."

Then on Friday, his JROTC class instructor handed students their uniforms, which resemble those of the U.S. armed forces, but did not give one to Bel. His father said the college student concluded it was because of the device strapped around his ankle.

"He came home that day feeling very bad," Pierres Ronal Bel said through an interpreter.

The younger Bel's next asylum court hearing was scheduled for October. He did not want to return to his home country because he was afraid of the rampant violence, according to Vilés Dorsainvil, executive director of the Haitian Support Center in Springfield, which is supporting the family.

On Monday morning, he left his family's home and placed a video call to his father at 8:03 a.m.

"'I'm not feeling okay,'" Pierres Ronal Bel recalled his son stating. "I told him to come so that we can talk."

Hours later, he said police officers arrived at his door to report that his son "threw himself under a truck."

Community leaders consoled Bel's parents at their home Monday evening. His solemn father gave interviews with reporters, and his mother wailed from an upstairs room. Residents have been banding together to support Haitian neighbors and call for an end to ICE's enforcement campaign against them.

Carl Ruby, a pastor who leads a Springfield congregation and advocates for Haitian immigrants, said he was struggling to make sense of the younger Bel's untimely death.

"I know that I'm a pastor and I'm supposed to be forgiving," he said. "But right now as I sit with a broken family, I'm crying out to God for righteous judgment in those who made this happen."

If you or someone you know needs help, visit 988lifeline.org or call or text the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988.

articles.title: Final German 'Dragon' submarine on its way to Israel as Navy continues modernization efforts
articles.summary: Multiple foreign publications have reported that Israeli submarines are part of a triad of nuclear deterrence that Israel possesses. The final of six submari...
articles.body:
Multiple foreign publications have reported that Israeli submarines are part of a triad of nuclear deterrence that Israel possesses.

The final of six submarines that Germany manufactured as part of a long-ago signed deal is on its way to Israel, the IDF and the Defense Ministry announced on Tuesday night.

Israeli Navy Chief V.-Adm. Eyal Harel and German Naval Chief Jan Christian Kaack, as well as other top Israeli and German officials, attended a send-off ceremony for the submarine earlier this week.

In February of this year, Elbit Systems released a strikingly vague statement about the beginning of joint work in Israel with the German maritime vessel manufacturing giant TKMS (the successor company to an expanded ThyssenKrupp and produced this submarine) to produce "structural components" for future submarines.

As part of the cooperation, Elbit said at the time that it would establish a new manufacturing facility for underwater GRP (Glass Reinforced Polyester) components for submarines.

Yoram Shmuely, general manager of the Aerospace Division at Elbit Systems, said, "This cooperation will expand local manufacturing capabilities and serve as an anchor for global activity in the underwater domain."

In December 2025, with Germany about to deploy its Arrow air defense system, bought from Israel, for the first time, Israel's Defense Ministry made new progress regarding the German-built submarines in Berlin, The Jerusalem Post reported at the time.

What can the German 'Dragon' submarines do?

According to foreign reports, the submarines can deliver nuclear weapons. Multiple foreign publications have reported that Israeli submarines are part of a triad of nuclear deterrence that Israel possesses, along with land-based and air-based weapons.

During Defense Ministry Director-General Amir Baram's stay in Germany , along with other senior defense officials, they made new progress regarding the ongoing submarine deals, which have unique offensive and defensive capabilities.

Though Israel has never publicly admitted to possessing nuclear weapons, former prime ministers – such as Ehud Olmert and others – have, at times, slipped up and alluded to the weapons program.

Besides the offensive dimensions, the IDF made unusual disclosures about the involvement of submarines in operations against Iran, Yemen, and Syria during the Israel-Hamas War, including operations that assisted with Israel's defense against aerial threats.

Movement on both the submarines and the Arrow, along with new levels of Israeli and German cooperation in other cutting-edge technologies, such as artificial intelligence, signaled in December 2025 that the special relationship between Berlin and Jerusalem remained despite disagreements over the Gaza war.

In November 2024, then-IDF Naval chief V.-Adm. (ret.) David Saar Salame named the new "Dragon" submarine at a ceremony in Germany.

At the time, it was thought that Israel would receive the submarine in late 2025.

The navy has carried out surveillance and struck Hezbollah targets in several areas deeper into Lebanon than where IDF ground forces have progressed, given that those forces are limited to southern Lebanon.

In addition, the navy has provided constant defense to Israel's maritime borders and to its strategic sites, such as its natural gas rigs.

This has included clandestine operations that can reveal Hezbollah and other countries' plans to threaten or prepare to fire on Israel, but before they actually fire, it enables the air force to preemptively strike such enemy locations.

One especially challenging area has been defending against Houthi attacks on Eilat, given that when the navy helps shoot down threats, it must contend with an extremely small zone of defense so as not to invade Egyptian or Jordanian airspace – or it would need to coordinate with those countries if necessary.

The submarine deal dates back many years and has been part of the navy's strategic modernization effort.

articles.title: Cleveland Police to get £2m after A66 crash unleashes crimes
articles.summary: The home secretary says the money will help support the force in the aftermath of the A66 crash.
articles.body:
A police force is being given an extra £2m to tackle serious crime after the death of two police officers and five young men in a crash unleashed a spate of crimes, the home secretary has announced.

Shabana Mahmood pledged the funding after Prime Minister Andy Burnham paid tribute to the officers killed, and in light of the challenges faced by Cleveland Police following the seven deaths on the A66 near Middlesbrough on 22 August.

PC Matthew Blades and PC Tom Clough died when a Volkswagen Passat going the wrong way on the A66 at South Bank hit their vehicle. The five men in the Volkswagen also died.

The force has since arrested 27 people for activities linked to "serious and organised crime".

About 200 police officers from outside Cleveland Police have been drafted in to help the force tackle organised crime following the crash.

In the days following the deaths, police dealt with a series of incidents including homes being rammed and vehicles set on fire at a vigil.

Mahmood said "lawlessness of any kind" would "never be tolerated".

"In light of the situation the force has faced, we will allocate an additional £2m to Cleveland Police to tackle serious crime in the area," she said.

She paid tribute to the two officers who died in the A66 crash and said she recognised how "unnerving" the current climate would be for the "law abiding citizens" in the community.

She said: "We will do our best to support the Middlesbrough community, which is hurting and grieving right now, and we hear the call from the members of this house representing it for a discussion about investment in policing and police numbers."

Conservative MP Chris Philp told Mahmood the extra £2m pledged was "wholly inadequate" and said he was concerned about a shortfall in funding for the force in general.

He said: "This lawless gang chaos should never have been allowed to take root in the first place."

Commenting following the announcement, Cleveland's Labour Police and Crime Commissioner (PCC) Matt Storey said a "one-off payment" was "not a solution".

He said: "It does nothing to address the chronic underfunding that has disadvantaged policing in Cleveland for years."

He called on the government to act to address "deep-rooted funding inequalities".

"Cleveland Police needs at least an additional £20m every year to recruit and retain 200 more police officers, to strengthen efforts to crack down on serious and organised crime."

Speaking in the Commons, Mahmood said she was committed to reviewing the funding formula, which is used to determine the funding that each force is given.

She added the previous government had taken away 20,000 police officers from forces nationally.

The Labour MP for Middlesbrough and Thornaby East, Andy McDonald, told Mahmood that Cleveland Police had the highest rate of crime for any police force in England and Wales.

He said the latest figures showed about 123 recorded crimes per 1,000 residents, yet the force had received the "largest percentage reduction" in officers since 2010.

"Police numbers are not the only factor, but a force facing the highest demand in the country needs the resources to respond," he said.

He added the £2m would address some of the extra funding needed but he wanted to discuss how funding shortfalls could "urgently and permanently be corrected".

Mahmood said she would be happy to meet with MPs in the area to discuss the issue and wider funding concerns.

Luke Myer, Labour MP for Middlesbrough South and East Cleveland, also called for the government to review how funding was assigned.

Mahmood said "reviewing and reforming" the formula was "absolutely critical" and said she would be updating MPs on a schedule for changes to be discussed, once an independent review on police force structures had been completed.
