articles.title: Israel says Hamas security chief captured as strikes kill four during Gaza raid
articles.summary: The Israeli military says it carried out strikes in Gaza City during a raid by special forces to capture the head of Hamas's internal security service.
articles.body:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said Israeli special forces captured the head of Hamas's internal security service in a ground operation in Gaza.

Netanyahu said the man, whom he did not name, was "engaged in attempts to restore Hamas's governance in Gaza and in deception concerning the demilitarisation of the Strip".

Israel's military and Shin Bet security service said a special forces unit arrested him in Gaza City on Tuesday and then took him to Israel for questioning.

Israeli air strikes carried out during the raid killed at least four Palestinians, including two children and a woman, medics said. Hamas condemned Israel's actions as a "grave crime" and violation of their ceasefire.

On Tuesday morning, Palestinians in the crowded Katiba area of western Gaza City reported heavy Israeli bombardment, with two vehicles hit and turned to wreckage.

Videos captured chaotic scenes, with the sound of gunfire and the aftermath of strikes.

"A jeep stopped in the middle of the street and started firing indiscriminately left and right. It carried on firing at us like rain for more than 15 minutes," Wafika al-Helou, who lives in a tent in the area, told AFP news agency. "It was terrifying."

Another witness, Mutaz Abu Asr, said there were five or six strikes in less than three minutes.

Palestinian media reported that Israeli special forces and Israel-backed Palestinian militiamen opposed to Hamas entered the area, but that their presence was discovered. Some Israeli media suggested that only a local armed militia operated on the ground.

A Palestinian security source told the BBC the target of the Israeli operation was a senior official in the Hamas internal security service.

A spokesman for Gaza's Hamas-run government media office, Ismail al-Thawabta, said: "An Israeli special forces unit attempted to carry out a security operation in Gaza City, but the unit was exposed while carrying out the mission."

The ensuing Israeli strikes "resulted in a number of people being killed and others injured, in addition to the deaths of several members of the special forces unit", he added.

Later, Hamas issued a statement saying that the Israeli raid and strikes in a densely populated area constituted "a serious crime, a deliberate disregard for the lives of civilians, and an extension of the brutal war of annihilation against our people in the Gaza Strip".

On Tuesday evening, the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) and Shin Bet announced in a joint statement that Shin Bet special forces "entered a structure in the Gaza City area and apprehended the head of Hamas' Internal Security in the Gaza Strip".

"During the operation, the Israeli Air Force struck several targets in the area in order to remove threats to the forces. No IDF injuries were reported," they said.

Israel's prime minister commended the special forces for what he called the "daring operation" to arrest Hamas's internal security chief near his home.

"He is one of the most senior Hamas leaders, and was responsible for concealing and transporting our hostages, for sheltering senior Hamas figures, and for military build-up and attempts to restore the capabilities of the terror organisation," Netanyahu added.

In a separate incident on Tuesday, hospital officials in central Gaza said a Palestinian girl was killed by gunfire from Israeli troops east of the town of Deir al-Balah.

The IDF also said it had carried out a strike on a commander of Hamas's military wing in the Jabalia area, north of Gaza City, stressing that he had posed an immediate threat.

Gaza's Hamas-run Civil Defence rescue service said one of its first responders was seriously injured in a strike that targeted a person who had been passing by his station in Jabalia.

The Gaza war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage.

Since then, more than 73,460 people have been killed in Gaza, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.

articles.title: A Los Angeles theatre opened in 1932, then spent 15 years being rebuilt; its nearly $40 million restoration has finally brought the 729-seat landmark back
articles.summary: US News: In 1932 a brand new theater opened in South Los Angeles showing movies and live shows to a growing neighborhood. Decades later, after years of decline.
articles.body: In 1932 a brand new theater opened in South Los Angeles showing movies and live shows to a growing neighborhood. Decades later, after years of decline and closure, that same building sat dark and deteriorating, its ornate interior hidden behind boards and dust. In 2011, the city of Los Angeles committed to saving it, launching a restoration that would stretch over 15 years and cost nearly $40 million. Now, in 2026, the 729-seat Vision Theatre is finally reopening as a fully restored performing-arts centre, ready to host concerts, films, community events and local artists once again. This story draws on updates from the Los Angeles Department of Cultural Affairs and reporting from the Los Angeles Times on the theatre’s long journey back to life. Read on to know more:A landmark born in the Depression eraThe Vision Theatre, originally known as the Leimert Park Theatre, opened in 1932 in the heart of the Leimert Park village, a planned community in South Los Angeles. Designed in the Spanish Colonial Revival style, it featured a striking façade, decorative tilework, wrought-iron details and a grand auditorium with a high ceiling and classic proscenium stage.For decades, the theatre served as a cultural hub for the neighbourhood, screening first-run films and hosting community gatherings.But it, like many single-screen venues across the U.S., faced increasing pressure from multiplexes, changing demographics and evolving entertainment habits in the latter half of the 20th century.By the 1990s, the building had closed, and over time it fell into serious disrepair.Years of uncertainty and a plan to save itBy the 2000s, the Vision Theatre was widely recognised as a historic landmark, but its future was far from secure. The structure suffered from water damage, outdated systems and years of neglect. Demolition was sometimes discussed, while other proposals called for partial reuse that would have altered the building’s character.In 2011, the City of Los Angeles made a decisive move: it committed to restoring the theatre as a cornerstone of the Leimert Park Cultural and Arts District.The Vision Theatre was designated as a key asset in the city’s broader strategy to support South L.A. arts organisations, expand cultural programming and revitalise the Leimert Park village.What followed was a complex, multi-phase project that would take far longer and cost far more than anyone initially expected.15 years of restoration The Vision Theatre’s restoration spanned about 15 years, dictated by funding cycles, construction challenges and the need to balance historic preservation with modern performance standards.The total price tag approached $40 million, funded through a combination of city capital, state grants, private donations and philanthropic support.Key elements of the work included: Structural repairs to address seismic vulnerabilities and long-term water damage; restoration of historic features such as decorative plasterwork, tile, ironwork and the original marquee; upgrades to mechanical, electrical and plumbing systems to meet current codes and improve energy efficiency; installation of modern stage lighting, sound and rigging to support professional productions; and accessibility improvements, including new restrooms, seating arrangements and entry upgrades.Throughout the process, the city and its partners emphasised that the goal was not to create a museum piece, but a working theatre that could serve artists and audiences for decades to come.A 729-seat home for South L.A. artsWhen it reopens in 2026, the Vision Theatre will offer 729 seats across a restored auditorium with improved sightlines, acoustics and comfort. The space is designed to host a wide range of events including live music, from jazz and R&B to hip-hop and classical; theatre productions, dance performances and film screenings; and community meetings, lectures and cultural festivals.The theatre will be managed as part of the city’s Cultural Affairs Department portfolio, with programming developed in close collaboration with local arts organisations, Leimert Park merchants and community stakeholders. The intent is to make the Vision a true neighbourhood asset, not just a destination for occasional events.Why this matters for Leimert Park and South L.A.Leimert Park has long been a cultural centre for Black Los Angeles, home to bookstores, galleries, jazz clubs and a tight-knit community of artists and activists.The neighborhood has been under pressure over the years from disinvestment, gentrification and loss of important cultural spaces.For many residents, the Vision Theatre’s restoration is more than a building project; it’s a statement about the value of South L.A. culture and the city’s commitment to preserving it. By investing nearly $40 million and 15 years of work, Los Angeles is signalling that historic theatres in predominantly Black and Latino communities deserve the same level of care and attention as those in more affluent areas.The theatre is also expected to bring economic benefits to the village, drawing visitors for shows and events who will support nearby restaurants, shops and galleries.Challenges along the wayThe road to reopening was not smooth. The project faced delays due to funding gaps and changing city budgets; construction complications as crews uncovered additional damage once walls and ceilings were opened; and the need to constantly balance historic preservation requirements with modern safety and accessibility standards.Neighbors and arts advocates were sometimes frustrated with the pace, worried the theater might never reopen in their lifetimes.But city officials and project managers maintained that cutting corners would undermine the long-term viability of the building.What comes nextWith construction essentially complete, the focus now shifts to programming and operations. The city and its partners are working to:Book a mix of local, regional and national acts that reflect the diversity of South L.A.Develop educational and youth programmes that use the theatre as a teaching space.Ticket prices and dates should ensure that the venue remains accessible to residents living in the immediate area. As with all historic venues, the building will also require ongoing maintenance and periodic upgrading to keep it in great condition.A second act for a historic stageWhen the Vision Theater opened in 1932, it was a symbol of modern entertainment and community pride. After decades of decline and 15 years of reconstruction, its 2026 reopening marks a second act, one that blends respect for the past with a clear eye toward the future.For a neighbourhood that has seen too many cultural spaces close, the Vision’s return offers something rare: a large, professionally equipped venue that belongs to the community and is dedicated to the arts. As the lights come up and the curtain rises again, the 729-seat landmark is ready to write a new chapter in South Los Angeles’ cultural story.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Methodist university denies operating 'hidden' DEI program after undercover video posted of school official
articles.summary: Undercover video captures a Southern Methodist University staffer describing efforts to keep DEI hidden under a "cultural intelligence" label.
articles.body: An official at Southern Methodist University was captured on undercover video describing what she called "a lot of maneuvering" surrounding the school’s diversity, equity and inclusion efforts, according to footage released by Accuracy in Media that purports to show how DEI initiatives continued under different names. The video, shared Monday by school choice activist Corey DeAngelis, alleges SMU renamed its Office of Diversity and Inclusion the Office of Cultural Intelligence as part of an effort to keep DEI programming less visible. The SMU staff member, who is identified in the video by Accuracy in Media as Danielle Palomo, coordinator for community engagement, social change and intercultural engagement division of student affairs, said, "As you can probably imagine, we've had to do a lot of maneuvering in order to remain kinda hidden under a lot of things. But as long as we can keep doing what we're doing even to a smaller capacity, that is what we're going to do. We're going to do our best." JUSTICE DEPARTMENT LAUNCHES TITLE VI INVESTIGATION INTO DEI PROGRAMS AT ARIZONA STATE UNIVERSITY In the video, an undercover journalist asks Palomo, "I was hoping to see if y'all had any existing, like, equity trainings that maybe y'all provide for staff faculty and that would give us an idea of what to go off of." Palomo responded, "So, all of that is held through our Office of Cultural Intelligence. As you can probably imagine, we've had to do a lot of maneuvering in order to remain kind of hidden under a lot of things. But my office in particular, we do — we have had trainings like that in the past with students. TRUMP DEI CRACKDOWN ‘MISSES CORE IDEOLOGY' AND MUST TARGET LINGERING DANGER ON CAMPUSES, WATCHDOG WARNS "It's not going to be as severe, hopefully, as some of the other public universities have had to deal with, but I know that the university is definitely finding its like 'P's and Q's' and it's slowly like working to like rename things and maybe do away with things," Palomo said in the video. While SMU is a private university, it holds 164 active federal grants totaling nearly $30 million from agencies, including the departments of Defense, Health and Human Services, and Education, according to a May 2025 report by its independent student newspaper, The Daily Campus. FLORIDA STATE UNIVERSITY HIT WITH FEDERAL CIVIL RIGHTS INVESTIGATION OVER RACE, SEX-BASED SCHOLARSHIP PROGRAMS The outlet also reported that SMU’s research and development spending has more than tripled since 2010, rising from $18.7 million that year to nearly $59.8 million in fiscal year 2023. The Trump administration has moved to restrict DEI initiatives at federally funded schools through executive actions and Department of Education directives, though federal judges have blocked portions of those efforts amid constitutional and procedural challenges. DOJ OPENS PROBE INTO PRESTIGIOUS COLLEGE OVER ALLEGED DISCRIMINATION FAVORING MINORITY STUDENTS The Department of Education has also warned state education departments they must remove diversity, equity and inclusion policies or potentially lose federal funding. In a statement to Fox News Digital, a spokesperson for SMU said, "SMU does not operate a hidden Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) program. The university does offer activities under the Cultural Intelligence framework that was originally adopted in 2017. Cultural Intelligence focuses on the ability to learn from and understand different perspectives, strengthen relationships and foster mutual respect and community." "Through this approach, we equip members of our university community with the skills to communicate, lead, teach, coach and innovate effectively across different perspectives and experiences," the spokesperson added. "As with all university programs, SMU regularly reviews its practices to ensure they align with applicable legal requirements and our institutional mission." In a statement to Fox News Digital, school choice activist Corey DeAngelis said, "The Trump administration should pull every dollar of federal funding from universities that keep pushing DEI after pretending they shut it down. The radical left running these campuses is not rooting out Marxist DEI ideology. They are moving the goalposts, renaming offices and hiding the same agenda under new labels like ‘cultural intelligence.’ CONFIDENCE IN HIGHER EDUCATION SLIPS AFTER BRIEF RECOVERY, GALLUP POLL FINDS "SMU tuition is $63,736. Parents might be surprised to learn they are paying that much for a Christian university that is still pushing divisive far-left ideology. SMU also takes more than $25 million in federal funding each year. "A school charging that kind of tuition does not need taxpayer money to keep DEI alive under another name. If they want to keep the ideology, they can do it without federal funds." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Fox News Digital reached out to Palomo for comment.

articles.title: India on board, SCO reiterates condemnation of Iran attacks
articles.summary: India News: Expressing deep concern over developments in \"the Middle East and around Iran\", SCO member-states, including India, reiterated the bloc's condemnation.
articles.body: Expressing deep concern over developments in "the Middle East and around Iran", SCO member-states, including India, reiterated the bloc's condemnation of military strikes on Iranian territory that resulted in numerous civilian casualties and significant damage to Iran's economy, said the Bishkek Declaration Tuesday.India also joined other member-states in expressing condolences over the death of former Iranian supreme leader Ali Khamenei at the SCO summit in Bishkek.This was the second time that the SCO denounced the strikes on Iran after the war started on Feb 28, the first being in an early March standalone statement that called the attacks unacceptable. India had endorsed that statement too, even though bilaterally it has not explicitly condemned the attacks on Iran the way it has the missile and drone strikes on GCC countries.However, unlike the Tianjin Declaration last year that had condemned the June 2025 US and Israeli strikes on Iran, the Bishkek Declaration did not name the US and Israel. "Such actions violate the principles and norms of international law and the UN Charter and create serious risks to international peace and security," said the declaration. India and others backed Iran's sovereignty, advocating a resolution to the conflict solely through political and diplomatic means.They welcomed all efforts aimed at de-escalating the situation and noted that the only possible way to ensure peace and stability in the region is a comprehensive and just settlement of the Palestinian question. PM Narendra Modi met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on the margins of the SCO summit Monday and backed expansion of ties with Tehran, while the latter sought India's help to end the war. After distancing itself from a statement by SCO in June last year condemning Israel's strikes, India has signed on to joint documents by the bloc censuring the US-Israel military action against Iran.The declaration reflected a major Indian concern as it strongly condemned terrorism in all its forms, emphasised that "double standards" in the fight against terrorism are unacceptable and called on the international community to combat terrorism, including cross-border movement of terrorists. It called for UN playing a central role by fully implementing relevant UN Security Council resolutions and the UN Global Counter-Terrorism Strategy in accordance with the UN Charter and principles of international law to jointly combat all terrorist groups."Member states, reaffirming their firm commitment to combating terrorism, separatism, and extremism, emphasise the inadmissibility of attempts to exploit terrorist, separatist, and extremist groups for selfish purposes.," said the declaration.Targeting use of economic sanctions by the West, leaders also came out in support of a fair multilateral trading system focused on the framework established by WTO, while slamming unilateral coercive measures. "Member states oppose unilateral coercive measures ... that are detrimental to the interests of ensuring international security, including its food and energy, and that have a negative impact on the global economy."Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Clavicular leaving Kick for Twitch? His ‘deal’ claim sparks fan debate
articles.summary: US Streamers News: Braden “Clavicular” Peters says he could move from Kick to Twitch within a week, adding that he has a deal with Twitch. He made the announcement durin.
articles.body: Braden “Clavicular” Peters says he could move from Kick to Twitch within a week, adding that he has a deal with Twitch. He made the announcement during a stream after a viewer asked when he would start streaming on Twitch. A clip of the exchange was later shared on X, drawing reactions from viewers. Clavicular has around 430,000 followers on Kick, where he has built an audience. His Twitch plans have now become a talking point among fans, with some questioning what the reported deal means and whether the move will happen as described.Braden “Clavicular” Peters says Twitch switch could happen soonDuring the stream, a viewer asked Clavicular, “When are the Twitch streams?” He replied:“We’re gonna switch over to Twitch in, like, f**k, I don’t know. No, no, no. We’re gonna switch to Twitch to stream, just in general. We’ll do that, like, in a week or so. I don’t know. I haven’t decided yet.”The answer left the timing unclear, but Clavicular then gave a more direct response when another viewer asked whether Twitch had offered him a deal.“Yeah, I have a deal.”That claim has added another part to the story. Clavicular has not publicly shared the terms of the deal in the material available around the announcement. His official X account also recently said he had a “great talk” with the Twitch team about bringing his streams to the platform, with an announcement expected soon.At the same time, his Kick presence remains active. Kick’s official Clavicular page lists more than 430,000 followers, while recent streams have continued to appear on the channel. He continues to use Kick for recent livestreams. That means the latest comments do not, by themselves, establish that he has already ended his time on Kick.Fans question Braden “Clavicular” Peters’ Twitch dealThe Twitch announcement quickly split viewers. Some fans focused on how long Clavicular might last on the platform, while others questioned whether the reported deal was really an official Twitch agreement.“Ngl WE might be getting banned within the first few streams.” X user @ClaviUpdates said.“Definitely getting banned the first stream.” X user @ghjhcchjjj70839 commented.Another viewer argued that streaming on Twitch and having a formal deal with the platform are two different things.“He didn’t sign a deal with Twitch. He will be streaming on Twitch there is a difference. Anyone can stream in twitch without being signed.” X user @ExecuteOrder6_6 added.Other reactions were even more doubtful. One X user claimed Clavicular’s move was linked to lower Kick viewership, while another suggested his payout had fallen. Those claims were fan speculation and were not backed by confirmed figures in the material reviewed for this report.For now, the clearest update is that Clavicular says he has a Twitch deal and expects to begin streaming there soon. The exact terms of that deal, the start date and whether Kick will remain part of his streaming plans have not been fully explained.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
